docs.text: How do I fix import errors? ¤ Import errors can occur with locations or assets . This guide helps you troubleshoot and fix common import problems. Quick navigation ¤ Jump to the section you need: Location import errors Location hierarchy errors Location referenced data errors Asset import errors Asset hierarchy errors Asset referenced data errors Common issues across all import types Date and CSV formatting errors Location import errors ¤ Location imports are error-prone because of parent-child relationships and hierarchies. Location hierarchy errors ¤ Hierarchy imports require careful attention to parent-child relationships. Parent locations not created first ¤ Child locations can't be created if their parent doesn't exist yet. Example : You can't create "Ice Cream Plant A > Production Building > Filling Line 2" if "Ice Cream Plant A" and "Production Building" don't exist. What to do : Import locations in order: Top-level locations first (Ice Cream Plant A) Second-level locations next (Production Building) Lowest-level locations last (Filling Line 2) TODO: Add visual content A diagram showing location hierarchy structure (parent → child relationships) would be useful here. Incorrect object structure ¤ Location hierarchies require specific object structure in the import file. What to do : Use the system's location hierarchy template or export an existing hierarchy to see the correct format. Incorrect hierarchy relationships ¤ Parent-child relationships must be defined correctly in the import file. What to check : Parent location IDs are correct Hierarchy levels are properly defined System location references are valid What to do : Verify all parent locations exist before importing child locations . Import hierarchies sequentially Hierarchies require sequential loading (top → down). Import parent locations first, then their children. Location referenced data does not exist ¤ Location imports fail when they reference supporting records that don't exist in the system. What to check : GL account exists and is valid Service address is defined Calendar and shift are configured Failure class is set up Bill-to or ship-to address for the site is correct Classification or specification is available What to do : Create or correct the referenced record, or update the import file to use an existing value Make sure values in the import file match system values exactly (case-sensitive) Verify spelling and IDs are correct 💡 Tips for successful location imports ¤ Import hierarchies in order : Parents before children Verify referenced data : Check that supporting records exist Start with a template : Export existing records to see correct format Validate data first : Check all values against system data Use text format : Prevent Excel from corrupting data Test with small batches : Verify format before importing thousands of records Asset import errors ¤ Asset imports fail due to object structure , data issues, or missing referenced records. TODO: Add visual content A screenshot showing typical asset import error messages would be useful here. Common asset import problems and solutions ¤ Table 1. Common asset import problems and solutions ¤ Problem What happens Solution Parent doesn't exist Child asset fails Import parents first Excel corrupts IDs Leading zeros removed Format as text in Excel Missing required fields Record skipped Validate all required fields Invalid status codes Import fails Use valid status values File too large Timeout or failure Break into smaller batches Asset hierarchy errors ¤ If using parent-child asset relationships, hierarchy errors can cause import failures. What to check : Parent asset exists before importing child assets Parent asset ID is correct in the import file Parent asset exists at the expected site and location What to do : Import parent assets before child assets or subassemblies Verify that each child asset references the correct parent asset Confirm the parent asset location matches expectations Asset referenced data does not exist ¤ Asset imports fail when they reference supporting records that don't exist in the system. What to check : GL account exists and is valid Service address is defined Calendar and shift are configured Failure class is set up Rotating item is created (if applicable) Vendor or manufacturer exists Type value is valid Classification or specification is available What to do : Verify that referenced records exist in the system Correct spelling, IDs, and values in the import file Create missing referenced records before importing assets Revalidate the file before importing again 💡 Tips for successful asset imports ¤ Verify referenced data : Check that supporting records exist Start with a template : Export existing records to see correct format Validate data first : Check all values against system data Use text format : Prevent Excel from corrupting data Test with small batches : Verify format before importing thousands of records Common causes of asset import failures ¤ Wrong object structure ¤ The import file must match the expected object structure exactly. What to check : File structure matches ASSET object All required fields are included Field names are correct What to do : Use a template or export an existing asset to see the correct structure. Missing mandatory fields ¤ Assets have required fields that must be populated. Common required fields : Asset ID Description Site Status What to do : Review the import file to ensure all mandatory fields have values. Data errors in file ¤ Problems with the data itself cause import failures. Common data errors : Invalid status codes Non-existent site references Incorrect data types (text in number fields) Invalid dates What to do : Validate data against system values before importing. TODO: Add visual content A screenshot of an error file showing validation failures would be helpful. Why are only some asset records imported? ¤ Partial imports happen when some records pass validation and others don't. Import limits are exceeded : Some systems have limits on: Number of records per import File size Processing time What to do : Break large imports into smaller batches (for example, 1,000-5,000 records at a time). Errors stop processing mid-file : If a critical error occurs, the import might stop processing remaining records. What to do : Review error logs to identify where processing stopped, fix the error, and re-import remaining records. Validation failures block individual records : Each record is validated independently. Invalid records are skipped while valid ones are imported. What to do : Review the error file, fix failed records, and import them separately. Common issues across all import types ¤ Date values are invalid or reformatted ¤ Date formatting is a common source of import errors across all record types. Common causes : Excel changed the date format automatically The file uses mixed date formats (for example, MM/DD/YYYY and DD/MM/YYYY) The date format is ambiguous (for example, 01/02/2026) Date values do not match the expected import format What to do : Format date columns as text in Excel before entering values Use one consistent date format throughout the file Re-export or use a template to confirm the expected format Test a small import that includes date values before importing the full file Excel formatting corrupts data ¤ Excel can corrupt data in several ways: Dates : Converts text to dates (01-02 becomes Jan 2) IDs : Removes leading zeros (001 becomes 1) Long numbers : Converts to scientific notation What to do : Format all columns as text in Excel before entering data, or use a plain text editor to create the CSV. TODO: Add visual content A screenshot showing Excel formatting options (Format Cells → Text) would be helpful. Lack of pre-validation leads to late errors ¤ Without validation, errors aren't discovered until after processing starts. What to do : Always use the preview/validation function before committing the import. Parent-child relationships missing or loaded in wrong order ¤ Importing child records before parents causes failures. What to do : Sort your import file so parent records come before child records. Why shouldn't I load very large datasets in a single file? ¤ Bulk imports have constraints when loading very large volumes in a single batch. Constraints ¤ UI session timeouts : Long-running imports can time out in the web interface. Not designed for massive single-file batches : CSV imports work best with manageable batch sizes (typically under 5,000 records per file). Better suited for smaller datasets : For large imports, consider: Breaking into smaller batches (files under 5,000 records) Loading parent records before child records in separate files Using Data Management to monitor and track import status What happens next? ¤ To resolve import failures: Review error logs and error file Fix data issues in source file Ensure parent records exist for hierarchies Verify referenced data exists Preview/validate before importing Process the corrected import Verify records were created successfully Continue building your skills ¤ Verify the system is working ¤ Once your data is loaded, check whether the system is performing as expected. What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ How do I prepare data for import? What is the correct load order? How do I get data into the system? How do I standardize data? Still stuck? ¤ If this page did not answer your question: Browse all Q&A: Get answers In the product: Click the help icon (?) in the top right For a specific field: Click the field name or press Alt+F1

docs.text: Excel can corrupt data in several ways: Dates : Converts text to dates (01-02 becomes Jan 2) IDs : Removes leading zeros (001 becomes 1) Long numbers : Converts to scientific notation What to do : Format all columns as text in Excel before entering data, or use a plain text editor to create the CSV. TODO: Add visual content A screenshot showing Excel formatting options (Format Cells → Text) would be helpful.

docs.text: Without validation, errors aren't discovered until after processing starts. What to do : Always use the preview/validation function before committing the import.
docs.title: Lack of pre-validation leads to late errors

docs.text: Importing child records before parents causes failures. What to do : Sort your import file so parent records come before child records.

docs.text: How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? ¤ Understanding how locations , assets , and work orders connect helps you work more efficiently in Maximo Application Suite Select. docs.text: How do inspections work? ¤ An inspection is a set of questions that you answer about an asset or a location . Inspections use two apps: Inspection Forms , from Planning > Inspection Forms . Use it to define the forms that inspections use. Inspections , from Work Orders > Inspections . Use it to conduct inspections and record the results. Inspections is also in IBM Maximo Mobile, so you can inspect an asset or location where it is. The app has the same name on the desktop and in IBM Maximo Mobile. [SME confirmation required: Confirm that the inspection behavior in this topic applies to MAS Select. The source is the Maximo Manage documentation. Confirm that Inspection Forms and Inspections are the app names and locations in Select.] How inspections fit together ¤ A form defines the questions for an inspection. When the form is activated, an inspection appears in the Inspections app. An inspector answers the questions and completes the inspection. The results are saved with the asset or location that was inspected. [SME confirmation required: Confirm how inspections are scheduled or generated from a form in Select, and where the results appear for the asset or location.] What you can do in Inspections ¤ Filter your inspections by pending, in progress, and completed. Conduct several inspections at the same time, as a batch. Create an unscheduled inspection when you find something that is not on your schedule, including for several assets or locations at once. Show only the required questions, or only the questions that you have not answered. Review your answers in a summary before you complete the inspection. View the results of completed inspections. Attach photos to an inspection. Create follow-up work from an inspection. The app saves your answers automatically as you go. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. docs.text: What happens when I'm offline in IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile keeps working when your device loses its connection. The app stores your data on the device, so you can keep working and sync your changes later. [SME confirmation required: Confirm that the offline and sign-in behavior in this topic applies to MAS Select. The source is the Maximo Manage documentation.] How online and offline work ¤ Online: The app is connected to the server. It saves the data it retrieves to your device and keeps that data in sync with the server. You can also sync manually. Offline: The app is not connected to the server. It uses the data that is stored on your device. When the connection returns, the app syncs your changes automatically. Some features need a connection. For example, you must be online to use Assist and Parts Identifier. When is my device offline? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile treats your device as offline when any of these conditions apply: The device is in airplane mode. The network adapter of the device is turned off. The network bandwidth is low. The server cannot be reached from the device. Your sign-in session has expired. Signing in and staying signed in ¤ First sign-in: You need a network connection the first time you sign in. You use the same credentials that you use on the desktop. The app then creates a local data store on your device. Opening the app: Each time you open the app, it asks for your device's security credentials before it opens your local data. Session expiry: After your session expires, the app asks you to sign in again. If you do not sign in, you work offline until you do. By default, access expires after 30 minutes and the session can be renewed for up to 12 hours. Signing in again: To sign in at any time, select the cloud icon on the app screen. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the session lengths and the cloud icon in Select. The values given are the Maximo Manage defaults.] Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Online and offline ¤ Online Offline Data source The server and the data stored on your device The data stored on your device Syncing Automatic. You can also sync manually. Automatic when the connection returns Assist and Parts Identifier Available Not available [SME confirmation required: Confirm whether Assist and Parts Identifier are available in Select.] What to do next ¤ How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? : Download the app and sign in. docs.text: What is an asset ? ¤ An asset is any piece of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure that your organization maintains. Assets are the physical things you work on. Examples of assets ¤ Production equipment : Batch Mixer MX-01, Filler FL-02, Conveyor CV-02, Spiral Freezer SF-01 Process equipment : Pumps, motors, compressors, heat exchangers, chillers Facilities : HVAC systems, refrigeration units, lighting systems Vehicles : Trucks, forklifts, pallet jacks Storage : Tanks, silos, cold storage units Why assets matter ¤ Track maintenance history for each piece of equipment Schedule preventive maintenance Monitor asset condition and performance Plan for replacements and upgrades Calculate total cost of ownership Asset hierarchy ¤ Figure 1: Sample asset hierarchy for an ice cream manufacturer An asset is a physical piece of equipment that you maintain. You can organize assets in a parent-child hierarchy to show how equipment is connected and to track maintenance at the correct level. In figure 1, Batch Mixer MX-01, Filler FL-02, Conveyor CV-02, and Spiral Freezer SF-01 are parent assets . Parent assets can include child assets . For example, Batch Mixer MX-01 includes the Agitator motor and Seal. Assets are installed in locations , which show where the equipment operates. Using asset hierarchies has many benefits: Understand how equipment is related Track maintenance for a complete system or a specific component See both what the equipment is and where it is installed Want to see how this connects to locations and work orders ? See How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? Naming assets ¤ ✓ Do Use a short alphanumeric asset number Write a clear, specific description Use a consistent description format Identify the parent asset when relevant ✗ Don't Don't use vague descriptions such as PUMP Don't overload the asset number with too much detail Example assets : Batch Mixer MX-01, Filler FL-02, Conveyor CV-02, Spiral Freezer SF-01. Example descriptions : Filler FL-02, cone filling station; Batch Mixer MX-01, vanilla mix preparation. Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is a work order ? What is a location ? How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? How do I track asset history?

docs.text: What is a location ? ¤ A location is a physical place where work is performed or assets are installed. Locations help you organize and find equipment. Types of locations ¤ Operating locations : Where assets are installed and running Storerooms : Where parts and materials are kept Service locations : Customer sites or service areas Staging areas : Temporary locations for work preparation Why locations matter ¤ Find equipment quickly Organize maintenance by area Assign work by location Track costs by facility or department Plan work routes efficiently Manage access and safety Location hierarchy ¤ Figure 1: Sample location hierarchy for an ice cream manufacturer A location is a fixed place where work happens or where assets are installed. You can organize locations in a parent-child hierarchy to show how areas in a facility are connected and to track work in the correct place. In figure 1, Production Building is a parent location within Ice Cream Plant A. Parent locations can include child locations . For example, Production Building includes Mixing Room, Filling Line 2, and Packaging Zone. Cold Storage and Main Storeroom are separate locations in the same site . Want to see how this connects to assets and work orders ? See How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? Naming locations ¤ ✓ Do Use a unique location identifier Name locations so they make sense in the hierarchy Use location names for places, not equipment ✗ Don't Don't use the location name to represent the asset Don't mix place names and equipment names at the same hierarchy level without a clear reason Example names : Ice Cream Plant A, Production Building, Mixing Room, Filling Line 2, Packaging Zone, Cold Storage, Main Storeroom. Location vs. asset ¤ Location : The place, such as Filling Line 2 Asset : The equipment, such as Filler FL-02 Relationship : Asset is installed at location Some work orders are for locations , such as Clean production floor, rather than specific assets . Locations vs service addresses ¤ Locations and service addresses work together but serve different purposes. A location represents an operational place. A service address provides the physical or geographic details needed to find it. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Location terminology ¤ Term What it is Location An operational place where assets are used, stored, or repaired Service address The physical or geographic details needed to find that place or its associated assets Table 2. Detailed comparison of locations vs service addresses ¤ Aspect Location Service address Primary purpose Represents a place where assets are operated, stored, or repaired Provides detailed physical or geographic information that helps people find an asset or location Role in the data model Supports asset tracking, work management, purchasing, and the history of asset movements and performance at particular sites Provides another way to search for assets and locations and helps direct field crews to where work must be performed Structure Can belong to one or more location systems, which organize locations into logical parent-child hierarchies Can participate in an address system that establishes address ancestry and determines how addresses apply to child records Information stored Can include location type, status , associated assets , parent and child locations , and an associated service address Can include an address code, street information, coordinates, directions, landmarks, and other detailed location information Relationship to assets Assets can be installed at or associated with the location One service address can represent the position of one or more assets or physical locations Use on work records A location can identify where work is associated operationally When work is created for an asset or location , its service address can be copied to the service request or work order Example ¤ Consider an ice-cream manufacturing plant: Location : Packaging Line 2 : This record represents the operational place where equipment is installed and work is managed. It might be a child of the Packaging Area in the primary location hierarchy. Service address: Building B, south entrance, second floor, coordinates X/Y : This record provides the physical details that help a technician find Packaging Line 2. The service address does not replace the location . It supplements the location with address, navigation, or geographic information. How they work together ¤ A location can have an associated service address. You can add service addresses to assets , locations , work orders , and service requests. When work is created for an asset or location , the service address can be copied to the work order or service request. If an asset or location does not have its own service address, the system can use the address of the closest ancestor in the address hierarchy. A service address provides an additional way to find individual assets and locations , or groups of them. Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is an asset ? What is a work order ? How do locations , assets , and work orders work together?

docs.text: What is a work order ? ¤ A work order is a request or instruction to perform maintenance work. It's the central document that tracks everything about a maintenance job. Types of work orders ¤ Corrective maintenance : Fix something that broke Preventive maintenance : Scheduled routine maintenance Predictive maintenance : Work based on condition monitoring Project work : Installations, upgrades, modifications Inspections : Regular checks and assessments Why work orders matter ¤ Assign work to the correct people Track what work was done Record labor hours and costs Document parts used Maintain history of all maintenance Measure performance and productivity Work order lifecycle ¤ Created : The work order is the working record for the job. It captures what needs to be done, where the work happens, how urgent it is, and any instructions the technician will need later. Approved : Approval means the work can move ahead. At this point, planned items can be reserved and the planned cost and rate information for the job is recorded. Assigned : Before work starts, check that the right person owns the job and has the schedule, instructions, parts, and tools needed to do it. In Progress : Use this stage when physical work has actually started. Record labor , materials, services, and tools as the work happens so the record stays accurate. Completed : Use this when the physical work is finished. The record can still need final review or closeout, and some setups can move the work order forward automatically when assignments are completed. Closed : Closing finalizes the record. Unused item reservations are removed and the job becomes part of maintenance history. Hover over a stage in the diagram to see its description. Figure 1: The lifecycle of a work order in Maximo Application Suite Select A work order records maintenance work. It tells you what needs to be done, where the work happens, and which asset the work applies to. In this example, the work order Inspect filler nozzles is linked to Filler FL-02 at Filling Line 2. It also shows the work type and the parts used. This helps you track maintenance clearly and keep a useful history of the work performed. Want to see how this connects to locations and assets ? See How do locations , assets , and work orders work together? Naming work orders ¤ ✓ Do Let Maximo Application Suite Select create the work order number automatically Write the description as a clear, action-oriented summary ✗ Don't Don't use vague descriptions such as Broken or Need fix Don't treat the description and work type as the same thing Example names : Inspect filler nozzles; Replace seal on Batch Mixer MX-01; Quarterly inspection, Spiral Freezer SF-01. Work order vs. work request ¤ Work request : Someone reports a problem or need Work order : Approved request with assigned resources Not all requests become work orders - some may be rejected, combined, or deferred. Ready to work with work orders ? See How do I complete a job? for step-by-step guidance.

docs.text: Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? ¤ You can work with work orders in three places: The Work Orders application, from Work Orders > Work Orders . The Technician app on the desktop, from Work Orders > Technician . The Technician app in IBM Maximo Mobile. All three work with the same work orders . This happens because Maximo Application Suite Select includes two kinds of apps: Desktop applications , such as Work Orders, Assets , and Inventory . These are the full applications that match the rest of the interface. Role-based apps , such as Technician, Inspections, and Asset Manager. Each is built around the work that a role does every day, and each has a more modern layout. Apps such as Technician and Inspections are designed for IBM Maximo Mobile, where you can also work offline. IBM Maximo Mobile contains all of them. They also appear in the desktop menu with the same names, so the experience is the same on your computer and on your phone or tablet. The two kinds of apps do not match one for one. For example, Technician combines parts of several desktop applications into one app for completing work. Which one should I use? ¤ There is no fixed rule. Use the one that suits how you work: If you use IBM Maximo Mobile often, use apps such as Technician on the desktop too. You keep the same experience in both places. If you rarely use IBM Maximo Mobile, you might prefer desktop applications such as Work Orders. They are more consistent with the rest of the interface. Most of the menu is desktop applications. Only a smaller set of apps, such as Technician and Inspections, is also in IBM Maximo Mobile. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Apps in the desktop menu and IBM Maximo Mobile ¤ App Find it in the menu Use it to Technician Work Orders > Technician Complete assigned work. Inspections Work Orders > Inspections Complete inspections. Inspection Forms Planning > Inspection Forms Work with inspection forms. Asset Manager Assets > Asset Manager Look up and manage assets . Issues and Transfers Inventory > Issues and Transfers Issue and transfer inventory . Inventory Counting Inventory > Inventory Counting Count inventory . Service Requests Go to Service Requests Create and track service requests. Work Order Summary Go to Work Order Summary Review a summary of work orders . You can also use the search box at the top of the menu to find any app by name. [TO DO: Add the menu locations of Service Requests and Work Order Summary.] [SME confirmation required: Confirm the purpose of each app in the "Use it to" column.] Which apps can I see? ¤ The apps you see depend on the security group that your administrator assigned to you. For the security groups , see How do I add users? Table 2. Apps in the desktop menu and IBM Maximo Mobile, by security group ¤ Security group Apps System admin Service Requests Supervisor Technician, Inspections, Inspection Forms, Work Order Summary, Service Requests, Asset Manager Technician Technician, Inspections, Service Requests, Asset Manager Requester Service Requests Inventory clerk Issues and Transfers, Inventory Counting, Service Requests [SME confirmation required: Confirm this table against the security group descriptions in "How do I add users?". The security group descriptions are the source of truth. Technicians were given Inspections because they complete inspections. Confirm the other rows, including Service Requests for system admins and inventory clerks, and Inspection Forms for supervisors.] Note Technician is both a security group and an app. The Technician security group is a role that you assign to a user. The Technician app is one of the apps that role can use. What to do next ¤ Technician: Complete your first work order : Complete a work order . How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? : Get the app that contains Technician, Inspections, and the other apps in Table 1. How do I add users? : Assign the security group that gives a user access to apps. Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is a work order ? What can I do in my role?

docs.text: Why do some terms differ from what I'm used to? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select uses a consistent set of terms to describe assets , locations , work, and inventory . These might differ from the terms you use today or in other systems. If you're not sure what a term means, click any underlined term in this help center to see its definition and related terms. This list brings those definitions and common alternatives together in one place. Assets and equipment ¤ Asset ¤ Any piece of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure that your organization maintains. You might know this as: equipment, machine, or unit Want to know more? What is an asset ? · How do I classify assets ? · How do I track asset history? Work and maintenance ¤ Work order ¤ A request or instruction to perform maintenance work. It records what needs to be done, where, who did it, what parts were used, and how long it took. This record stays with the asset as part of its maintenance history. You might know this as: maintenance order, job, ticket , or work request Want to know more? What is a work order ? · How do I complete a work order ? Plan tab ¤ The Plan section of a work order is where you record what is expected before work starts: the tasks to perform, materials to request, and labor needed. When actual work happens, those details are recorded separately in the Actuals section. Comparing plan to actuals lets you see whether jobs came in on time and on budget. You might know this as: planned work, work plan, or expected materials Work log ¤ A record of notes and updates added directly inside a work order . Use the work log to describe what you found, what you did, and anything else the next person needs to know. Entries are time-stamped and show who wrote them. You might know this as: job notes, maintenance notes, or technician notes Communications log ¤ A record of emails, notifications, and messages sent or received in connection with a work order . The communications log captures the conversation around the work, such as approval requests, status updates, and alerts. It is separate from the work log, which is for internal notes. You might know this as: message history, notification log, or email log Preventive maintenance ¤ Scheduled routine maintenance performed to prevent equipment failures. You might know this as: maintenance plan, planned maintenance, or PM Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance? Corrective maintenance ¤ Maintenance performed to fix equipment that has broken down. You might know this as: breakdown maintenance, repair work, or reactive maintenance Want to know more? How do I decide what work should be done? · What happens when an asset fails? Job plan ¤ A template that defines standard tasks, materials, and labor for recurring maintenance work. You might know this as: standard job, task template, or maintenance procedure Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance? Status ¤ The lifecycle state of a work order or record. You might know this as: lifecycle state, order state, or workflow stage Want to know more? How do I complete a work order ? Locations and sites ¤ Location ¤ A functional location or operating area where assets are installed or work is performed. You might know this as: functional location , area, or site area Want to know more? What is a location ? Site ¤ A data partitioning concept that represents a plant, facility, or business unit. You might know this as: plant, facility, or business unit Want to know more? What are the basic concepts? People, roles, and access ¤ Person and role ¤ A person record holds an individual's contact details and is used across the system to identify who owns, supervises, or reports on work. A role, also called a security group , determines what applications and actions that person can access. When you add a user, you assign them to a security group . The security group defines the role. The person record and the user account are separate, though they are linked. You might know this as: user type, access level, or permission group Want to know more? How do I add users? · How do I assign the correct people? Security group ¤ A collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. You might know this as: permission group, access group, user group, or role Want to know more? How do I add users? Authorized users ¤ The number of authorized users defines how many people are entitled to access the product under your subscription. When you add a new user account, it counts against this limit. If you reach the limit, you cannot add more users until entitlement is increased. Contact your IBM account representative to adjust your authorized user count. You might know this as: licensed users, named users, or seat count People and skills ¤ Labor ¤ Work time and effort assigned to a work order . You might know this as: technician time, work hours, or crew time Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Craft ¤ A trade or skill type required for maintenance work. You might know this as: trade, skill type, or discipline Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people? Inventory and materials ¤ Inventory ¤ Materials and spare parts stored for maintenance work. You might know this as: stock, stores, or warehouse Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job? Item and material ¤ An item is the master record for a part or material in the catalog, such as a filter or a seal. Material is the same thing in the context of a work order : materials are items requested or used for a specific job. The word changes depending on where you are in the system, but they refer to the same physical thing. You might know this as: spare part, stock item , or consumable Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job? Material request, reservation, and issue ¤ These three terms describe the sequence of getting parts to a job: Material request : You identify the parts needed for a job and add them to the work order plan. This is a signal of intent, not a commitment. Reservation : When the work order is approved, the system can reserve the requested items in the storeroom. A reservation holds the stock so it is not allocated to another job before yours. Issue : When you physically take the parts and use them, you issue them against the work order . This deducts the quantity from inventory and records the cost. You might know this as: pick list, parts request, stock allocation, or materials withdrawal Rotating item ¤ A repairable spare part that can be tracked individually by serial number. You might know this as: repairable spare, rotable, or serialized spare Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? Tracking and monitoring ¤ Meter ¤ A counter that tracks equipment usage, such as hours, cycles, or miles. You might know this as: counter, runtime meter , or odometer Want to know more? How do I detect issues early? Failure code ¤ A standardized code used to categorize and track equipment failures. You might know this as: failure classification, breakdown code, or fault code Want to know more? What happens when an asset fails? Downtime ¤ The period when equipment is not operational or available for use. You might know this as: outage, production loss, or equipment unavailable Want to know more? How do I reduce downtime ? · How do I detect issues early? Service requests ¤ Ticket ¤ A service request or incident report. You might know this as: service request, incident, or request Want to know more? What are the basic concepts? Configuration and data ¤ Object structure ¤ Defines the records and related fields that are available for importing, exporting, or exchanging data. You might know this as: data structure, import template, or record definition Want to know more? Which object structure do I use for each data type? · How do I get data into the system? Domain ¤ A list of valid values attached to a field that controls what users can select in a dropdown. You might know this as: value list, lookup list, or picklist Want to know more? How do I customize dropdown values? Communication template ¤ A reusable email template that can be triggered automatically by a workflow or escalation , or manually from a record. You might know this as: email template, notification template, or message template Want to know more? How do I automate communication? Escalation ¤ An automated rule that monitors the system for a condition and performs an action or sends a notification when that condition is met. You might know this as: alert rule, automated notification, or trigger Want to know more? How do I automate communication? · How do I act on alerts? People and teams ¤ Crew ¤ A named group of workers assembled to complete a job together, assigned as a team to a work order . You might know this as: work crew , team, or work gang Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people? Data sync ¤ The process of transferring record, lookup, and map data between the server and a mobile device. You might know this as: synchronization, offline sync, or data refresh Want to know more? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? User interface ¤ Default application ¤ The application that opens when a user logs in. Users can set their own default application in their profile preferences. Administrators can also set defaults for a security group . Choosing the correct default means users land on the most relevant application for their role without extra navigation. You might know this as: home screen, landing page, or startup application Start Workflow ¤ A workflow is an automated sequence of steps that routes a record through an approval or review process. "Start Workflow" is the action that begins this process for a specific record. Once started, the record follows a defined path, such as routing a work order to a supervisor for approval, and the system handles the routing automatically. You might know this as: submit for approval, begin approval process, or route for review Share with admin ¤ The "Share with admin" action sends a copy of information or a report to a system administrator. Administrators receive the information and can act on it, such as reviewing a configuration issue or adjusting access. The exact content and outcome depends on where in the system you use the action. You might know this as: send to admin, notify administrator, or escalate to admin API calls ¤ An API call is a request your system makes to Maximo Application Suite Select to exchange data automatically. For example, sending a new work order from an external system counts as one API call. Subscription plans include a defined number of API calls per period. If you integrate other systems with Maximo Application Suite Select, each data exchange uses some of this allowance. You might know this as: system integrations, data requests, or integration transactions Upgrade ¤ In Maximo Application Suite Select, Upgrade refers to moving to a higher subscription tier or adding capacity to your account. This gives you access to additional features, more users, or higher usage limits. You might know this as: subscription upgrade, plan upgrade, or adding capacity Basemap ¤ The background map layer that shows geography, streets, or satellite imagery. You might know this as: background map, base layer, or map tile Want to know more? How do I set up maps? Operational dashboard ¤ A landing page to monitor KPIs, manage upcoming assignments, complete tasks, or access related applications. You might know this as: command center, control panel, or operations console Want to know more? What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ What are the basic concepts? What is an asset ? What is a work order ? What is a location ?

docs.text: Any piece of equipment, machinery, or infrastructure that your organization maintains. You might know this as: equipment, machine, or unit Want to know more? What is an asset ? · How do I classify assets ? · How do I track asset history?
docs.title: Asset

docs.text: A request or instruction to perform maintenance work. It records what needs to be done, where, who did it, what parts were used, and how long it took. This record stays with the asset as part of its maintenance history. You might know this as: maintenance order, job, ticket , or work request Want to know more? What is a work order ? · How do I complete a work order ?
docs.title: Work order

docs.text: The Plan section of a work order is where you record what is expected before work starts: the tasks to perform, materials to request, and labor needed. When actual work happens, those details are recorded separately in the Actuals section. Comparing plan to actuals lets you see whether jobs came in on time and on budget. You might know this as: planned work, work plan, or expected materials
docs.title: Plan tab

docs.text: A record of notes and updates added directly inside a work order . Use the work log to describe what you found, what you did, and anything else the next person needs to know. Entries are time-stamped and show who wrote them. You might know this as: job notes, maintenance notes, or technician notes
docs.title: Work log

docs.text: A record of emails, notifications, and messages sent or received in connection with a work order . The communications log captures the conversation around the work, such as approval requests, status updates, and alerts. It is separate from the work log, which is for internal notes. You might know this as: message history, notification log, or email log
docs.title: Communications log

docs.text: Scheduled routine maintenance performed to prevent equipment failures. You might know this as: maintenance plan, planned maintenance, or PM Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance?
docs.title: Preventive maintenance

docs.text: Maintenance performed to fix equipment that has broken down. You might know this as: breakdown maintenance, repair work, or reactive maintenance Want to know more? How do I decide what work should be done? · What happens when an asset fails?
docs.title: Corrective maintenance

docs.text: A template that defines standard tasks, materials, and labor for recurring maintenance work. You might know this as: standard job, task template, or maintenance procedure Want to know more? How do I plan recurring maintenance?
docs.title: Job plan

docs.text: The lifecycle state of a work order or record. You might know this as: lifecycle state, order state, or workflow stage Want to know more? How do I complete a work order ?
docs.title: Status

docs.text: A functional location or operating area where assets are installed or work is performed. You might know this as: functional location , area, or site area Want to know more? What is a location ?
docs.title: Location

docs.text: A data partitioning concept that represents a plant, facility, or business unit. You might know this as: plant, facility, or business unit Want to know more? What are the basic concepts?
docs.title: Site

docs.text: A person record holds an individual's contact details and is used across the system to identify who owns, supervises, or reports on work. A role, also called a security group , determines what applications and actions that person can access. When you add a user, you assign them to a security group . The security group defines the role. The person record and the user account are separate, though they are linked. You might know this as: user type, access level, or permission group Want to know more? How do I add users? · How do I assign the correct people?
docs.title: Person and role

docs.text: A collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. You might know this as: permission group, access group, user group, or role Want to know more? How do I add users?
docs.title: Security group

docs.text: The number of authorized users defines how many people are entitled to access the product under your subscription. When you add a new user account, it counts against this limit. If you reach the limit, you cannot add more users until entitlement is increased. Contact your IBM account representative to adjust your authorized user count. You might know this as: licensed users, named users, or seat count
docs.title: Authorized users

docs.text: Work time and effort assigned to a work order . You might know this as: technician time, work hours, or crew time Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ?
docs.title: Labor

docs.text: A trade or skill type required for maintenance work. You might know this as: trade, skill type, or discipline Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people?
docs.title: Craft

docs.text: Materials and spare parts stored for maintenance work. You might know this as: stock, stores, or warehouse Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job?
docs.title: Inventory

docs.text: An item is the master record for a part or material in the catalog, such as a filter or a seal. Material is the same thing in the context of a work order : materials are items requested or used for a specific job. The word changes depending on where you are in the system, but they refer to the same physical thing. You might know this as: spare part, stock item , or consumable Want to know more? How do I track stock levels? · How do I issue parts to a job?
docs.title: Item and material

docs.text: These three terms describe the sequence of getting parts to a job: Material request : You identify the parts needed for a job and add them to the work order plan. This is a signal of intent, not a commitment. Reservation : When the work order is approved, the system can reserve the requested items in the storeroom. A reservation holds the stock so it is not allocated to another job before yours. Issue : When you physically take the parts and use them, you issue them against the work order . This deducts the quantity from inventory and records the cost. You might know this as: pick list, parts request, stock allocation, or materials withdrawal
docs.title: Material request, reservation, and issue

docs.text: A repairable spare part that can be tracked individually by serial number. You might know this as: repairable spare, rotable, or serialized spare Want to know more? How do I track stock levels?
docs.title: Rotating item

docs.text: A counter that tracks equipment usage, such as hours, cycles, or miles. You might know this as: counter, runtime meter , or odometer Want to know more? How do I detect issues early?
docs.title: Meter

docs.text: A standardized code used to categorize and track equipment failures. You might know this as: failure classification, breakdown code, or fault code Want to know more? What happens when an asset fails?
docs.title: Failure code

docs.text: The period when equipment is not operational or available for use. You might know this as: outage, production loss, or equipment unavailable Want to know more? How do I reduce downtime ? · How do I detect issues early?
docs.title: Downtime

docs.text: A service request or incident report. You might know this as: service request, incident, or request Want to know more? What are the basic concepts?
docs.title: Ticket

docs.text: Defines the records and related fields that are available for importing, exporting, or exchanging data. You might know this as: data structure, import template, or record definition Want to know more? Which object structure do I use for each data type? · How do I get data into the system?
docs.title: Object structure

docs.text: A list of valid values attached to a field that controls what users can select in a dropdown. You might know this as: value list, lookup list, or picklist Want to know more? How do I customize dropdown values?
docs.title: Domain

docs.text: A reusable email template that can be triggered automatically by a workflow or escalation , or manually from a record. You might know this as: email template, notification template, or message template Want to know more? How do I automate communication?
docs.title: Communication template

docs.text: An automated rule that monitors the system for a condition and performs an action or sends a notification when that condition is met. You might know this as: alert rule, automated notification, or trigger Want to know more? How do I automate communication? · How do I act on alerts?
docs.title: Escalation

docs.text: A named group of workers assembled to complete a job together, assigned as a team to a work order . You might know this as: work crew , team, or work gang Want to know more? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? · How do I assign the correct people?
docs.title: Crew

docs.text: The process of transferring record, lookup, and map data between the server and a mobile device. You might know this as: synchronization, offline sync, or data refresh Want to know more? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team?
docs.title: Data sync

docs.text: The application that opens when a user logs in. Users can set their own default application in their profile preferences. Administrators can also set defaults for a security group . Choosing the correct default means users land on the most relevant application for their role without extra navigation. You might know this as: home screen, landing page, or startup application
docs.title: Default application

docs.text: A workflow is an automated sequence of steps that routes a record through an approval or review process. "Start Workflow" is the action that begins this process for a specific record. Once started, the record follows a defined path, such as routing a work order to a supervisor for approval, and the system handles the routing automatically. You might know this as: submit for approval, begin approval process, or route for review
docs.title: Start Workflow

docs.text: The "Share with admin" action sends a copy of information or a report to a system administrator. Administrators receive the information and can act on it, such as reviewing a configuration issue or adjusting access. The exact content and outcome depends on where in the system you use the action. You might know this as: send to admin, notify administrator, or escalate to admin
docs.title: Share with admin

docs.text: An API call is a request your system makes to Maximo Application Suite Select to exchange data automatically. For example, sending a new work order from an external system counts as one API call. Subscription plans include a defined number of API calls per period. If you integrate other systems with Maximo Application Suite Select, each data exchange uses some of this allowance. You might know this as: system integrations, data requests, or integration transactions
docs.title: API calls

docs.text: In Maximo Application Suite Select, Upgrade refers to moving to a higher subscription tier or adding capacity to your account. This gives you access to additional features, more users, or higher usage limits. You might know this as: subscription upgrade, plan upgrade, or adding capacity
docs.title: Upgrade

docs.text: The background map layer that shows geography, streets, or satellite imagery. You might know this as: background map, base layer, or map tile Want to know more? How do I set up maps?
docs.title: Basemap

docs.text: A landing page to monitor KPIs, manage upcoming assignments, complete tasks, or access related applications. You might know this as: command center, control panel, or operations console Want to know more? What metrics matter?
docs.title: Operational dashboard

docs.text: Administrator: Add users ¤ Get started quickly with a task designed for administrators like you. Learn the basics while accomplishing something useful. Add a new user to the system and assign them appropriate access, for example, add users for Ice cream plant A. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Use consistent naming conventions for user IDs Follow principle of least privilege, that is, minimum access needed Keep security group assignments organized What to do ¤ Add a user ¤ Open the Users application. Click Create user . Specify a login email . Specify a user ID . Optionally, add a note in the memo . Example: Temporary access for contractor at ice cream plant A Provide a display name . This is the full name of the user or a recognizable preferred name. Click Select groups and add the user to at least one security group . An email is sent to the login email address. Table 1. Security groups ¤ A security group is a collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. A role determines what a person can see and do in Maximo Application Suite Select. Assign each user to the security group that matches their role: Security group What they can do System admin Manages system configuration and user access. System administrators can configure domains , communication templates , AI settings, create users, and set up security groups , but typically do not perform day-to-day operational work. Example tasks: Set up notification templates, manage user roles, set up security groups , configure system settings, and maintain data structures. Supervisor Oversees operations and team activities. Supervisors can plan and approve work, review technician work, monitor assets and performance, and access analytics to track progress. Example tasks: Assign and approve work orders , review KPIs, review inspection results, manage job plans , and monitor asset condition and maintenance schedules. Technician Performs maintenance and operational work. Technicians can view and update assigned work, complete inspections, record labor hours, report materials used, and record asset data such as meter readings and condition details. Example tasks: Complete work orders , enter inspection results, update asset condition, record labor hours, report materials used, and report meter readings. Requester Submits and tracks service requests. Requesters have limited access and cannot perform operational or administrative tasks. This role is focused on initiating and monitoring work requests. Example tasks: Create a service request for a broken asset and track its status until it is resolved. Inventory clerk Manages inventory and storeroom operations. Inventory clerks can maintain stock, process item movements, adjust inventory balances, and ensure accurate inventory records. Example tasks: Receive items into inventory , issue materials to work orders , perform inventory counts, adjust inventory balances, and manage storerooms. Note You must assign at least one security group . The user cannot access applications until a security group is assigned. User preferences ¤ Users update their preferences in their profile. They open the profile menu from the top right of the header and can select preferences, such as a default application , storeroom, locale, and language. What success looks like ¤ You've successfully added your first user when: User can log in successfully User sees appropriate applications and menus Security group permissions work as expected User can perform tasks for their role No error messages or access issues You'll know you're ready to move on when you can create users efficiently, assign appropriate permissions, and troubleshoot access issues independently. What's next? ¤ After creating your first user, try: Configuring email notifications Setting up additional security groups Need help? ¤ If you get stuck on your first task: Check Starting out for answers to common questions Review the basics in What are the basic concepts? Once you've added your first user, setting up the rest of your team follows the same steps — just repeated at scale. Continue building your skills ¤ Set up your workforce ¤ After adding users, create the craft and labor records that let you assign work to the correct people. How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Customize your dropdown values ¤ Add your organization's terminology to status fields and dropdowns so the system speaks your team's language. How do I customize dropdown values? Related links ¤ Edit settings How do I customize dropdown values? - Domains How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? - Calendars How do I automate communication? - Communication templates How do I set up maps? - Map manager How do I automate communication? - Push notifications administration How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? - Mobile configuration General How do I assign the correct people? What are the basic concepts?

docs.text: How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile lets you view assigned work, complete work orders , assign and approve work, issue parts, receive inventory , and update records from your phone or tablet. [TO DO: Confirm whether MAS Select includes the Receiving and Approvals apps. Maximo Manage includes both, but they are not on the Select menu. If Select does not include them, remove "receive inventory" and "approve work" here, in "What can I do in my role?", and in the inventory clerk first task.] Technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks all use IBM Maximo Mobile. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Download the app before your first shift, not during it. Sign in with the same credentials you use on the desktop. Sync your work list after signing in so your assignments are available on the device. What you need before you start ¤ A mobile device running iOS or Android. [TO DO: Confirm whether Windows devices are supported in Select. Maximo Manage supports iOS, Android, and Windows.] Your Maximo Application Suite Select login credentials. Your administrator must have configured IBM Maximo Mobile for your team. If the app is not yet available, contact your administrator. Download the app ¤ Open the App Store (iOS) or Google Play (Android) on your device. Search for IBM Maximo Mobile . Download and install the app. Sign in ¤ Your first sign-in needs a network connection. The app creates a local data store on your device, which it uses when you work offline. Open IBM Maximo Mobile on your device. If the app asks for a server URL, enter your Maximo Application Suite Select server URL. Your administrator can also set the URL for you, in which case the app does not ask. Enter your username and password. Tap Sign in . [SME confirmation required: Confirm the exact sign-in screens in Select, including single sign-on prompts.] Sync your work ¤ While your device is online, the app syncs your work automatically. You can also sync manually at any time. If your device is offline, the app uses the data stored on the device and syncs when it reconnects. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the name and location of the manual sync control in Select.] What to do next ¤ Technician: Complete a work order : Complete your first work order using the app or desktop. What happens when I'm offline in IBM Maximo Mobile? : Learn how the app works without a connection. Why can't I see new work in IBM Maximo Mobile? : Fix missing work on your device. How do I find my work? : Find and filter your assigned work queue. How do I complete a work order ? : Walk through the full work order completion workflow. Related topics ¤ Technician: Complete a work order How do I find my work? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team?

docs.text: Inventory clerk: Issue a part ¤ Get started quickly with a task designed for inventory clerks like you. Learn the basics while accomplishing something useful. Issue a part from the storeroom to a work order , for example, issue parts from Main storeroom. Guided steps available: Prefer to learn in the application? Log in and open your Operational dashboard to follow guided steps for issuing a part. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Always verify item numbers before issuing Keep storeroom organized and labeled Issue parts promptly to avoid work delays Record transactions immediately Check for reorder needs after issuing What to do ¤ Check for work orders needing parts. Review the parts list. Note the work order number. Go to Inventory application. Search by item number or description. Check the storeroom location . Verify quantity available. Go to the storeroom. Find the correct bin location . Verify the item number matches. Check the part condition. In Maximo, open the inventory record. Click Issue action. Enter the work order number. Specify quantity to issue. Confirm the transaction. Check that inventory balance decreased. Verify work order shows the material. Confirm cost was recorded. Hand over the physical part to technician. What success looks like ¤ You've successfully issued your first part when: Inventory balance decreased by the correct quantity Work order shows the material issued with cost Transaction recorded with work order number Physical part delivered to technician Storeroom bin location updated if needed System and physical inventory match No errors or warnings in the transaction You'll know you're ready to move on when you can issue parts quickly and accurately, verify inventory balances, and handle multiple requests efficiently. Get IBM Maximo Mobile ¤ Take your work with you. IBM Maximo Mobile lets you issue parts, receive inventory , and transfer items between storerooms from your phone or tablet. [TO DO: Confirm whether MAS Select includes the Receiving app. If not, remove "receive inventory" here.] How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? Every part you issue accurately means one less discrepancy to chase down later — good habits here make inventory reliable for everyone. Why can't I issue materials to a work order ? Know what you have ¤ Move beyond reacting to requests. Learn to monitor stock levels so you can see what's running low before it causes a delay. How do I track stock levels? Fix a discrepancy ¤ When the system and the shelf don't match, learn how to investigate and correct it before it causes a parts shortage. What happens if stock is incorrect? Monitor inventory performance ¤ Track stock-outs, turnover, and parts availability so you can stay ahead of what work needs and prevent delays. docs.text: Technician: Complete your first work order ¤ Get started quickly with a task designed for technicians like you. Learn the basics while accomplishing something useful. Find and complete an assigned work order , for example, complete work on Filler FL-02. Guided steps available: Prefer to learn in the application? Log in and open your Operational dashboard to follow guided steps for completing a work order . 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with a simple preventive maintenance task Ask your supervisor if you're unsure about anything Take photos to document your work Record information as you go, not at the end What to do ¤ Log into Maximo Application Suite Select. Go to Work Orders > Work Orders , or go to Work Orders > Technician and select Assigned work . The Technician app is also available in IBM Maximo Mobile. Learn Why can I manage work orders in more than one place? Choose a simple work order to start (look for status "Assigned" or "In Progress"). New to work orders ? Learn What is a work order ? to understand the basics. Click to open the work order details. Change status to "In Progress". Review what needs to be done. Check if you need any parts or tools. Perform the maintenance task. Add notes about what you did. Record time spent ( labor hours). Add any parts you used. Need to request parts? See How do I issue parts to a job? Update meter readings if applicable. Change status to "Completed". Verify all information is recorded. Submit for approval if required. What success looks like ¤ You've successfully completed your first work order when: Work order status changed from "Assigned" to "Completed" All required fields are completed such as notes, labor hours, or parts used Your supervisor can see what you did and why Equipment history now shows your work Parts inventory updated automatically Time and costs are recorded for planning You'll know you're ready to move on when you can complete a simple work order from start to finish without help, and your notes clearly explain what you found and fixed. For more detail on recording notes, parts, and time accurately, see How do I complete a work order ? What can I do in the Technician app? ¤ The Technician app, from Work Orders > Technician , is built around the work that you do every day. It is the same app on the desktop and in IBM Maximo Mobile. In the Technician app, you can: View the work orders that are assigned to you, and filter them by priority, status , or due date. View work orders on a map to plan routes and reduce travel time. See work details such as job plans , instructions, and safety requirements. Record labor hours, tool use, and material use. Update the work order status as you work. Attach photos, notes, and documents to work orders . Report failures and update failure class information. Request materials, tools, or services. View details of the related asset and location . Add to the work log and review earlier entries. Create follow-up work orders . Record meter readings, such as energy use, run time, or fuel level. [SME confirmation required: Confirm that this list matches the Technician app in Select. The source is the Maximo Manage documentation.] Get IBM Maximo Mobile ¤ Take your work with you. IBM Maximo Mobile lets you view assigned work, complete work orders , and update records from your phone or tablet. How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? Your first completed work order is the start of a reliable record — every one you complete after this adds to a history that helps the whole team work smarter. Continue building your skills ¤ Find your assigned work ¤ Before your next shift, learn how your work queue works so you always know what to do first. How do I find my work? Issue parts to a job ¤ When your work order needs materials, record them as you go so inventory stays accurate. How do I issue parts to a job? When something gets in the way ¤ Know what to do when you're blocked by missing parts, access issues, or a problem bigger than expected. What if I can't complete a task? Understand the equipment you're working on ¤ See the full maintenance history of any asset to spot patterns and avoid repeat failures. How do I track asset history? What happens when an asset fails? Pourquoi ne puis-je pas sortir des matériaux ? Pourquoi certains termes diffèrent-ils de ceux que j'utilise habituellement ? Pourquoi les techniciens n'utilisent-ils pas le système ? Quels sont les concepts de base ? ¤ Découvrez les éléments de base que vous utiliserez chaque jour : Qu'est-ce qu'un emplacement ? - Lieux physiques où le travail est effectué Qu'est-ce qu'un actif ? - Équipements, machines et infrastructures que vous entretenez Qu'est-ce qu'un ordre de travail ? - Instructions pour effectuer un travail de maintenance Comment les emplacements , les actifs et les ordres de travail fonctionnent-ils ensemble ? - Découvrez comment ces concepts s'articulent dans des scénarios réels Qu'est-ce que Maximo Application Suite Select ? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select est une solution SaaS (Software as a Service) prête à l'emploi. Aucune installation. Aucune configuration. Aucune personnalisation nécessaire. Il vous suffit de vous connecter et de commencer à travailler : Suivre les actifs Créer et terminer des ordres de travail Planifier la maintenance préventive Gérer l'inventaire des pièces Surveiller les performances À qui s'adresse-t-il ? ¤ Les techniciens peuvent rechercher et terminer des ordres de travail, par exemple terminer le travail sur Filler FL-02. Les superviseurs peuvent planifier, affecter et suivre le travail de maintenance, par exemple affecter la maintenance préventive de Spiral freezer SF-01. Les magasiniers peuvent gérer les pièces et les fournitures, par exemple sortir des pièces de Main storeroom. Les administrateurs peuvent charger des données et configurer des utilisateurs, par exemple charger des utilisateurs pour Ice cream plant A. À propos de ces exemples ¤ Pour faciliter la prise en main, les exemples de ce centre d'aide reposent sur un même scénario : une usine de fabrication de crèmes glacées. Vous retrouvez le même site , les mêmes emplacements, les mêmes actifs et le même travail, ce qui vous permet de vous concentrer sur l'enchaînement du flux de travail. Quels problèmes résout-il ? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select vous aide à passer d'une maintenance réactive de type « fonctionnement jusqu'à la panne » à une maintenance préventive et organisée : Ne perdez plus le fil du travail : tous les ordres de travail dans un seul système, et non dispersés dans des feuilles de calcul ou sur papier Évitez les pannes d'équipement : planifiez la maintenance avant que les problèmes ne surviennent Sachez ce que vous avez : suivez tous vos actifs et leur historique de maintenance Maîtrisez l'inventaire des pièces : voyez ce qui est en stock et ce qui a été utilisé Prenez de meilleures décisions : utilisez les données pour comprendre ce qui fonctionne et ce qui demande de l'attention Emportez votre travail avec vous ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile permet aux techniciens de consulter les actifs, de gérer les ordres de travail et de mettre à jour le travail depuis leur téléphone ou leur tablette, où que le travail soit effectué. Téléchargez IBM Maximo Mobile depuis l'App Store ou Google Play, puis connectez-vous avec vos identifiants Maximo Application Suite Select. Techniciens : consultez votre file de travail affecté, terminez des ordres de travail et enregistrez les données réelles en déplacement. Superviseurs : affectez et approuvez le travail depuis le terrain. Magasiniers : sortez des pièces, réceptionnez des stocks et transférez des articles entre magasins. Administrateurs : configurez IBM Maximo Mobile pour votre équipe avant que quiconque ne se connecte. Prenez en main le produit en quelques minutes ¤ Vous découvrez Maximo Application Suite Select ? Commencez ici : Que puis-je faire dans mon rôle ? Découvrir les notions de base Effectuer votre première tâche Trouvez ce dont vous avez besoin ¤ Démarrer rapidement ¤ Obtenez de la valeur dès les premières minutes. Explorer « Démarrer rapidement » → Accomplir le travail ¤ Effectuez les tâches de maintenance courantes. Explorer « Accomplir le travail » → Améliorer les résultats ¤ Rendez votre programme de maintenance plus efficace. Explorer « Améliorer les résultats » → Travailler plus intelligemment ¤ Utilisez l'intelligence artificielle (IA), l'automatisation et les analyses pour passer à l'échelle. Explorer « Travailler plus intelligemment » → Obtenir des réponses ¤ Trouvez rapidement des réponses aux questions courantes. Parcourir toutes les questions → Besoin d'aide ? ¤ Dans le produit : cliquez sur l'icône d'aide (?) en haut à droite Pour une zone précise : cliquez sur le nom de la zone ou appuyez sur Alt+F1 Vous ne trouvez pas de réponse ? : consultez la section Obtenir des réponses Prêt à commencer ? Vous retrouvez le même site , les mêmes emplacements, les mêmes actifs et le même travail, ce qui vous permet de vous concentrer sur l'enchaînement du flux de travail.

docs.text: Maximo Application Suite Select vous aide à passer d'une maintenance réactive de type « fonctionnement jusqu'à la panne » à une maintenance préventive et organisée : Ne perdez plus le fil du travail : tous les ordres de travail dans un seul système, et non dispersés dans des feuilles de calcul ou sur papier Évitez les pannes d'équipement : planifiez la maintenance avant que les problèmes ne surviennent Sachez ce que vous avez : suivez tous vos actifs et leur historique de maintenance Maîtrisez l'inventaire des pièces : voyez ce qui est en stock et ce qui a été utilisé Prenez de meilleures décisions : utilisez les données pour comprendre ce qui fonctionne et ce qui demande de l'attention

docs.text: IBM Maximo Mobile permet aux techniciens de consulter les actifs, de gérer les ordres de travail et de mettre à jour le travail depuis leur téléphone ou leur tablette, où que le travail soit effectué. Téléchargez IBM Maximo Mobile depuis l'App Store ou Google Play, puis connectez-vous avec vos identifiants Maximo Application Suite Select. Techniciens : consultez votre file de travail affecté, terminez des ordres de travail et enregistrez les données réelles en déplacement. Superviseurs : affectez et approuvez le travail depuis le terrain. Magasiniers : sortez des pièces, réceptionnez des stocks et transférez des articles entre magasins. Administrateurs : configurez IBM Maximo Mobile pour votre équipe avant que quiconque ne se connecte.

docs.text: Ajouter un utilisateur ¤ Ouvrez l'application Users. Cliquez sur Create user . Indiquez une adresse e-mail de connexion . Indiquez un ID utilisateur . Si vous le souhaitez, ajoutez une note dans le champ mémo . Exemple : accès temporaire pour un sous-traitant de l'usine de crèmes glacées A Indiquez un nom d'affichage . Il s'agit du nom complet de l'utilisateur ou d'un nom d'usage facilement reconnaissable. Cliquez sur Select groups et ajoutez l'utilisateur à au moins un groupe de sécurité. Un e-mail est envoyé à l'adresse e-mail de connexion. Tableau 1. Groupes de sécurité ¤ Un groupe de sécurité est un ensemble d'utilisateurs qui disposent des mêmes accès. Les droits d'un groupe de sécurité déterminent les applications, les actions et les données auxquelles ses membres peuvent accéder. Un rôle détermine ce qu'une personne peut voir et faire dans Maximo Application Suite Select. Affectez chaque utilisateur au groupe de sécurité qui correspond à son rôle : Groupe de sécurité Ce qu'ils peuvent faire System admin Gère la configuration du système et les accès des utilisateurs. Les administrateurs système peuvent configurer les domaines, les modèles de communication et les paramètres d'IA, créer des utilisateurs et définir des groupes de sécurité, mais ils n'effectuent généralement pas de travail opérationnel au quotidien. Exemples de tâches : configurer des modèles de notification, gérer les rôles des utilisateurs, définir des groupes de sécurité, configurer les paramètres système et gérer les structures de données. Supervisor Supervise les opérations et les activités de l'équipe. Les superviseurs peuvent planifier et approuver le travail, examiner le travail des techniciens, surveiller les actifs et les performances, et accéder aux analyses pour suivre l'avancement. Exemples de tâches : affecter et approuver des ordres de travail, examiner les indicateurs clés de performance, examiner les résultats d'inspection, gérer les plans de travail, et surveiller l'état des actifs et les calendriers de maintenance. Technician Effectue le travail de maintenance et le travail opérationnel. Les techniciens peuvent consulter et mettre à jour le travail qui leur est affecté, effectuer des inspections, enregistrer les heures de main-d'œuvre, déclarer les matériaux utilisés et enregistrer des données sur les actifs, comme les relevés de compteur et les détails sur l'état. Exemples de tâches : terminer des ordres de travail, saisir les résultats d'inspection, mettre à jour l'état des actifs, enregistrer les heures de main-d'œuvre, déclarer les matériaux utilisés et saisir les relevés de compteur. Requester Soumet et suit des demandes de service. Les demandeurs disposent d'un accès limité et ne peuvent pas effectuer de tâches opérationnelles ou administratives. Ce rôle consiste à lancer et à suivre des demandes de travail. Exemples de tâches : créer une demande de service pour un actif en panne et suivre son statut jusqu'à sa résolution. Inventory clerk Gère l'inventaire et les opérations du magasin. Les magasiniers peuvent tenir à jour les stocks, traiter les mouvements d'articles, ajuster les soldes d'inventaire et garantir l'exactitude des enregistrements d'inventaire. Exemples de tâches : réceptionner des articles en stock, sortir des matériaux pour des ordres de travail, effectuer des comptages d'inventaire, ajuster les soldes d'inventaire et gérer les magasins. Note Vous devez affecter au moins un groupe de sécurité. L'utilisateur ne peut pas accéder aux applications tant qu'aucun groupe de sécurité n'est affecté.
