docs.text: What metrics matter? ¤ Maximo Application Suite Select tracks maintenance performance through key performance indicators (KPIs). A KPI measures one specific variable over time, such as how many work orders were completed on schedule, or how long equipment typically runs before failing. The metrics that matter most depend on your role. A supervisor needs to know whether today's work is on track. An administrator needs to know whether the overall maintenance program is healthy. An inventory clerk needs to know whether parts are available when work demands them. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with three to five KPIs, not twenty. Too many metrics dilute focus and make it harder to act. Set thresholds for every KPI: a green target, a yellow caution level, and a red alert level. Without thresholds, a KPI is just a number. Review KPIs on a regular cadence that matches your role: daily for supervisors, weekly or monthly for managers and administrators. A KPI is only as reliable as the data behind it. If technicians are not closing work orders accurately, completion rate and MTTR figures will be wrong. What metrics matter to supervisors? ¤ Supervisors use KPIs to monitor daily work progress and respond to problems before they escalate. The Operational Dashboard for supervisors gives you a role-based view of the metrics most relevant to your team. Table 1. Supervisor metrics ¤ Metric What it tells you Where to find it Work order completion rate How many work orders were completed vs. scheduled in a given period. A low rate signals resource or planning problems. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor Overdue work orders Work that has passed its required finish date. Growing overdue counts mean scheduling or capacity issues. Operational Dashboard, Work Queues PM compliance The percentage of preventive maintenance work orders completed on schedule. Target is 85% or higher. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor Emergency work orders The count of unplanned, reactive work orders . High numbers indicate equipment is failing unexpectedly instead of being maintained proactively. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor Maintenance backlog The volume of outstanding work. A healthy backlog is 2 to 4 weeks of work. Above 6 weeks signals a resource problem. Work Queues Schedule compliance How often planned work is completed when it was scheduled. Targets above 90% indicate a well-run maintenance program. Operational Dashboard, Supervisor How supervisors use these metrics ¤ Review completion rate and overdue work orders daily. Use the Work Queues card on your Operational Dashboard to act on items directly. You can change status , assign work, or escalate without leaving the dashboard. What metrics matter to administrators? ¤ Administrators use KPIs to assess the health of the overall maintenance program and configure the system to support it. KPI Manager is where administrators create, configure, and manage KPIs for the organization. Table 2. Administrator metrics ¤ Metric What it tells you Where to find it Planned maintenance percentage (PMP) The ratio of planned maintenance hours to total hours. Above 80% means your program is proactive, not reactive. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Mean time between failures (MTBF) The average time equipment runs before failing. Rising MTBF means reliability is improving. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Mean time to repair (MTTR) The average time to repair an asset after failure. High MTTR indicates slow response or complex failures. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Asset availability The percentage of time an asset is operational. Critical for production equipment. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer Reactive maintenance ratio Emergency work orders as a percentage of total work. World-class programs keep this below 10%. KPI Manager, KPI Viewer KPI threshold breaches KPIs that have crossed caution or alert thresholds. These require investigation or program adjustments. KPI Manager How administrators use these metrics ¤ Use KPI Manager to create KPIs with defined targets, caution levels, and alert thresholds. Make frequently reviewed KPIs public so they appear on role-specific Operational Dashboards. Review program-level metrics monthly and adjust PM schedules or resource allocation based on trends. Three configuration points that are easy to miss: Set thresholds on every KPI. A KPI without a green target, yellow caution, and red alert level is just a number. The traffic-light colour coding on the Operational Dashboard only activates when thresholds are configured. Without them, supervisors see data but no signal. Make KPIs public. A KPI configured in KPI Manager is private by default. It will not appear on anyone's Operational Dashboard until you explicitly make it public or assign it to a security group . Activate new work queues. In Maximo Application Suite Select, a newly created work queue defaults to inactive. If a work queue shows no results on the Operational Dashboard, check that it has been activated in Work Queue Manager. What metrics matter to inventory clerks? ¤ Inventory clerks use metrics to ensure parts are available when work demands them. Stock-related KPIs help prevent delays caused by missing parts. Table 3. Inventory clerk metrics ¤ Metric What it tells you Where to find it Stock-outs How often a required part was unavailable when needed. Frequent stock-outs delay work and increase downtime . Operational Dashboard, Inventory Clerk Inventory turnover How quickly stock is consumed and replenished. Low turnover may mean overstocking; high turnover may indicate understocking. Operational Dashboard, Inventory Clerk Parts requested vs. available The gap between what technicians need and what is in stock. Helps prioritize reordering. Operational Dashboard, Inventory Clerk Where to find KPIs in the product ¤ Table 4. KPI applications ¤ Application Who uses it What it does KPI Manager Administrators Create, configure, and manage KPIs. Set targets, thresholds, and security group access. KPI Viewer All roles View individual KPI values and trends. Read-only access to configured KPIs. KPI Templates Administrators Create reusable templates to generate multiple related KPIs efficiently. Operational Dashboard All roles Role-based dashboard showing KPI trend cards, work queue cards, and alert summaries. Work Queue Manager Administrators Create and manage work queues that surface actionable items on the Operational Dashboard. Continue building your skills ¤ Act on what the data tells you ¤ When a KPI breaches a threshold, the Operational Dashboard surfaces it as an alert. Learn how to respond directly from the dashboard without leaving the view. How do I act on alerts? Catch problems before they become failures ¤ Condition monitoring feeds asset health data into your metrics. Set it up so your KPIs reflect equipment state, not just work order counts. How do I detect issues early? What to do next ¤ How do I act on alerts? : Use your Operational Dashboard to take action when KPIs breach thresholds. How do I plan recurring maintenance? : Improving PM compliance starts with a well-configured maintenance schedule. How do I detect issues early? : Condition monitoring feeds asset health metrics on your dashboard. Related topics ¤ How do I detect issues early? How do I act on alerts? docs.text: How do I assign the correct people? ¤ Match the right technician or crew to a work order so the job goes to someone with the correct skills, availability, and access. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Set up crafts and labor records before assigning work. A labor record without a craft won't appear when you filter by skill. See How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? if your workforce isn't configured yet. Check availability before assigning. The system shows scheduled hours and availability based on the labor record's calendar and shift. Use crews when multiple people need to work on the same job at the same time. Assigning a crew takes one step instead of adding each person individually. Set a scheduled start date on every assignment. Without a date, the assignment won't surface in scheduling views at the correct time for planning or dispatch. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Assignment methods ¤ Method Best for Work orders , Plans section Assigning an individual to a work order Crew assignment Assigning a whole team to a job in one step How to assign an individual to a work order ¤ What to do: Open the Work orders application. Search for and open the work order . Go to the Plans section. Under Assignment , click Edit assignments . In the Labor field, enter or select the person to assign. Enter the estimated hours in Time to complete . This is how the system calculates whether a person is over-allocated. Without it, the system shows unlimited availability for that slot and supervisors can unknowingly double-book people. Save the work order . Note Assignments filter by the default craft on the labor record. A person with the correct skill set as a secondary craft will not appear. If the list is empty or missing expected people, check that the correct craft is set as their default in the Labor application. How to assign a crew ¤ Use a crew when a group of people need to work together on the same job. What to do: Open the Work orders application. Search for and open the work order . Go to the Plans section. Under Assignment , click Edit assignments . In the Crew field, enter or select the crew name. The system adds all active crew members as individual assignments. Save the work order . Why isn't someone showing up as available? ¤ The most common reasons a technician doesn't appear in the Available Labor list: No craft assigned ¤ Available Labor filters by default craft only . A person with the correct skill as a secondary craft is excluded from the results — they exist in the system but the filter doesn't find them. What to do : Open the Labor application, find the person's record, and confirm the correct craft is set as their default, not just listed as a secondary craft . Calendar or shift mismatch ¤ Available Labor uses the calendar and shift on the labor record. If the scheduled start date falls outside the person's working hours, they may not appear or show as unavailable. What to do : Check that the calendar and shift on the labor record match the crew 's working schedule. Work order status doesn't allow assignment ¤ You can only assign labor to work orders in an approvable or approved status . Work orders in Waiting for Approval (WAPPR) or Approved (APPR) status accept assignments. What to do : Check the work order status and change it to APPR before assigning. Assigning the correct people consistently means work gets done faster and teams stop stepping on each other. Continue building your skills ¤ Understand why a technician can't see their assigned work ¤ After assigning work, verify it's visible to the correct people. Why can't technicians see their assigned work? Set up the workforce records behind assignments ¤ If assignments aren't working correctly, the issue is often in how crafts , calendars, and labor records are set up. docs.text: How do I customize dropdown values? ¤ Domains control the values users can pick from in dropdown lists and status fields across the application. As an administrator, you can add your own labels to existing status dropdowns to match your organization's terminology. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Domain terminology ¤ Term What it means Domain A list of valid values attached to a field, such as the values available in a work order status dropdown Synonym domain A domain used for status fields. Lets you add your own labels that map to built-in system statuses Internal value The system status that drives business logic, such as WAPPR (Waiting for Approval) or COMP (Complete) Synonym value A custom label you add that maps to an internal value, such as "Needs sign-off" mapping to WAPPR What you can do in IBM Maximo Application Suite Select ¤ Table 2. Domain customization tasks ¤ Task How Add a custom label to a status field Add a synonym value to an existing domain Use different terminology across your organization Set a synonym value at the organization level Find which domain controls a field Use Alt+F1 on the field, then look up the domain in Domains Why add synonym values? ¤ Synonym values let you use your organization's terminology without affecting how the system works underneath. For example, your team might call a work order status "Needs sign-off" rather than "Waiting for Approval." You can add "Needs sign-off" as a synonym that maps to the built-in WAPPR status . Users see your label. The system still processes work orders using the standard internal status . Common uses: Rename work order or asset statuses to match your organization's language Add organization-specific labels for a status Localize terminology for your team What you cannot change ¤ You can add synonym values, but you cannot add new internal values. The system's business logic — what happens when a work order reaches APPR, COMP, or CLOSE — is hardwired to those internal values and cannot be modified. If you need a status that behaves differently from any existing internal value, that is not possible through domain configuration. How to add a synonym value ¤ Go to System Configuration > Platform Configuration > Domains . Search for the domain you want to update. For example, search for WOSTATUS to find the work order status domain . Open the domain record. In the Values table, click Add Row (the + button above the values list). Leave the Internal Value field set to the existing system status you want to map to. Enter your custom label in the Value field. Add a description to explain the value. If this value applies to a specific organization only, set the Organization field. An organization-level synonym is visible across all sites in that organization. A value with no organization set applies system-wide. Choosing the wrong scope can expose values to users who should not see them, or hide them from users who need them. To make this the default value for the field, select Default . Click OK . Save the domain record. Before you add synonym values after go-live ¤ Adding synonym values at the organization level after your system is live can cause issues with existing records. If you add synonyms with an organization specified, records that were created before the change may no longer match valid values. If you need to add organization-scoped synonyms after go-live, add a synonym for every existing internal value at the same scope before saving. If you are unsure about the impact, test the change in a non-production environment first, or contact IBM support. How to find the correct domain for a field ¤ To identify which domain controls a specific field: Place your cursor in the field. Press Alt+F1 to open field help. The field name and domain name appear in the field help panel. Go to System Configuration > Platform Configuration > Domains and search for that domain name. Continue building your skills ¤ Set up maps for your field teams ¤ Visual maps let technicians and supervisors see where assets and work orders are located. Set up a map after your dropdown values are in place. How do I set up maps? Automate your notifications ¤ Keep your team informed automatically. Set up email and push notifications so people know when work is assigned or updated. How do I automate communication? docs.text: Why don't technicians see their assigned work? ¤ This is one of the most common issues. Work is assigned, but the technician can't see it in their queue. TODO: Add visual content A screenshot showing an empty work queue vs. a populated work queue would be useful here. Likely causes ¤ User permissions were updated but sessions weren't refreshed ¤ When permissions change, active sessions might not pick up the new access rights immediately. What to do : Have the technician log out of all sessions completely, then log back in. This forces the system to reload their current permissions. Clear all sessions Logging out of all sessions (including mobile devices and any open browser tabs) often resolves visibility issues immediately. Missing site or data access ¤ The technician might not have access to the site where the work order exists, or their data restrictions might prevent them from seeing certain work orders . What to check : Verify the technician has access to the correct site Check if data restrictions are limiting what they can see Confirm their security group includes the necessary permissions What to do : Contact your system administrator to review and update site access or data restrictions. Cached sessions not picking up new permissions ¤ Even after permissions are updated, cached session data might prevent the changes from taking effect. What to do : Have the technician: Log out completely from all devices Clear browser cache if using a web browser Close and reopen mobile apps Log back in Why can't I update assignment status ? ¤ You might see validation errors or the status doesn't save when you try to move from Assigned → Started → Complete. Status sequence skipped ¤ Some organizations require work orders to progress through specific statuses in order. You can't skip steps. Example : You can't go directly from "Assigned" to "Complete" without going through "In Progress" first. What to do : Follow the required status sequence for your organization. Date validation errors ¤ The system validates that dates make sense. Common issues: Finish date must be after start date Scheduled date must be after creation date Actual dates must align with planned dates What to do : Check all dates on the work order and correct any that are out of sequence. Updates not committing to the database ¤ Sometimes changes appear to save but don't actually commit to the database. What to do : Verify the change was saved by refreshing the screen Check for error messages that might have been missed Try the update again Contact your system administrator if the problem persists Why is it hard to track who is doing what? ¤ Supervisors often struggle with visibility into team workload and assignments. Known limitations ¤ Out-of-the-box views : Standard views don't easily show workload per technician Reporting complexity : Reports can include incorrect or excessive data Filtering behavior : Filters might not work as expected for assignment tracking What to do : Use custom queries or reports designed for your organization Ask your system administrator about available workload views Consider using dashboards that show team assignments TODO: Add visual content A screenshot showing a supervisor dashboard with team workload distribution would be useful here. Why do assignments disappear after work order completion? ¤ Assignments are typically removed when the work order is closed or completed. Impact ¤ No historical assignment tracking unless configured separately Reporting needs to rely on work order history instead of active assignments What to do : If you need historical assignment data, work with your system administrator to set up: Assignment history tracking Custom reports that capture assignment data before completion Archive processes that preserve assignment information What happens next? ¤ To resolve visibility issues: Have technicians log out and back in Verify site access and permissions Check data restrictions Clear cached sessions if needed Contact your system administrator if problems persist Continue building your skills ¤ Plan recurring maintenance ¤ With your team seeing their work correctly, set up schedules that generate work orders automatically so you're not creating them one at a time. How do I plan recurring maintenance? Know what work matters ¤ Create job plans that standardize tasks, parts, and time estimates so every technician does the work the same way. How do I decide what work should be done? Related topics ¤ How do I assign the correct people? Why can't I see new work in IBM Maximo Mobile? How do I find my work? How do I complete a job? Still stuck? ¤ If this page did not answer your question: Browse all Q&A: Get answers In the product: Click the help icon (?) in the top right For a specific field: Click the field name or press Alt+F1

docs.text: How do I decide what work should be done? ¤ Create job plans that list the steps, parts, and tools for common maintenance tasks. Job plans work like templates. They keep work consistent every time. You plan the work once. Then you reuse the plan. This saves time and reduces mistakes. TODO: Add visual content A diagram showing how job plans flow into work orders would be useful here. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with common tasks Create plans for work you do most often. Keep it simple Use clear, short instructions. Add safety notes Include warnings for dangerous work. Update regularly Change plans based on worker feedback. Use for all scheduled work Every maintenance schedule should have a job plan . When to use job plans ¤ Use job plans for: Tasks you do regularly (monthly inspections) Work with multiple steps Jobs that need specific parts or tools Tasks where safety matters Scheduled maintenance What goes in a job plan ¤ Include these items : Work description What you need to do and why. Task list Step-by-step instructions. Labor estimates How many people and hours you need. When this job plan is applied to a work order and the work order is approved, the system automatically creates assignment records for each labor entry. Without labor estimates, no assignments are created — planners must add them manually every time. Required materials Parts and supplies you need. When a work order with planned materials is approved, the system automatically creates storeroom reservations. Without materials on the job plan , no reservations are made and parts may not be available when the technician arrives on site . Tools Special equipment or tools. Safety information Hazards and safety steps. How to create and use job plans ¤ Create the job plan ¤ Open the Job Plans application Add a clear name and description List all work tasks in order Add labor , materials, and tools Set the WO Priority field. This pre-fills priority on every work order generated from this plan. Without it, work orders default to null priority and sort to the bottom of every scheduling and assignment view — urgent work becomes invisible to planners. Use with scheduled maintenance ¤ Attach job plans to your maintenance schedules. Work orders include the job plan automatically. Use with work orders ¤ Add job plans to individual work orders . Technicians see all steps and materials. Keep plans current ¤ Review completed work. Update job plans based on what actually happened. Add missing steps or materials. To change a job plan that is already active, select Revise Job Plan first. If you try to add or change tasks without revising the plan, you get the error "BMXAA0024E - The action ADD is not allowed on object JOBTASK." [SME confirmation required: Confirm where Revise Job Plan appears in the Job Plans application in Select, and whether other errors can appear when editing an active job plan.] TODO: Add visual content A video showing how to create a simple job plan would be useful here. Why job plans help ¤ Everyone does the work the same way No confusion about steps or procedures. Work goes faster No time spent figuring out what to do. You get the correct parts All materials are listed upfront. Reservations are created automatically at approval — no manual follow-up needed. Training is easier New workers have clear instructions. Costs are predictable You know time and materials in advance. Assignments are created for you Labor entries on the job plan generate assignment records when the work order is approved. The correct people appear in the assignment queue without a planner having to add them manually. Continue building your skills ¤ Schedule your team ¤ With job plans in place, set up calendars and routes so work is assigned when people are available and inspections run in sequence. How do I schedule work? Monitor performance ¤ Track whether work is being completed on time, how much backlog your team carries, and where to intervene. What metrics matter? docs.text: How do I plan recurring maintenance? ¤ Create a schedule that automatically generates work orders . The system creates work orders for you based on time (every 30 days) or equipment use (every 500 hours). This helps you maintain equipment before it breaks. You set up the schedule once. The system does the rest. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with a small number of critical assets (5-10), then expand once the process works reliably Always create job plans before setting up schedules. They ensure consistent work. Set lead times based on your actual parts procurement time plus a buffer (typically 7-14 days) Review completed work orders monthly and adjust schedules based on actual equipment performance Activate schedules gradually to avoid overwhelming your team with work orders When to use this ¤ Use recurring maintenance when you need to: Inspect or service equipment regularly Maintain equipment based on how much it runs Follow manufacturer maintenance schedules Prevent equipment breakdowns Keep consistent maintenance records How to set it up ¤ Step 1: Create a job plan (recommended) ¤ A job plan lists the work steps, parts needed, and time required. It keeps the work consistent every time. You can skip this step, but job plans make maintenance easier. Include in job plan Required when Task list The work has multiple steps that technicians must follow in order Labor entries You want assignment records created automatically at work order approval Material entries You want storeroom reservations created automatically at work order approval WO Priority This work must appear correctly sorted in scheduling views Step 2: Create the maintenance record ¤ Open the Preventive Maintenance application Choose the equipment or location Describe the maintenance work clearly Step 3: Set the schedule ¤ Choose how often to do the work: Time-based schedule Every 30 days Every 2 weeks Every 6 months Usage-based schedule Every 500 operating hours Every 1000 cycles Every 200 miles Combined schedule Every 6 months OR 300 hours (whichever comes first) Every year OR 1000 hours (whichever comes first) Fixed vs. floating: choose carefully ¤ This setting controls when the next work order is generated. Fixed schedule : The next work order is created on the calendar interval regardless of whether the previous one was completed. A monthly PM generates every 30 days, every time. Floating schedule : The next work order is not created until the previous one reaches a completed, closed, or cancelled status . If a work order is never closed, the PM stops generating entirely — with no warning. One missed closure can silently halt maintenance on an asset indefinitely. Use a fixed schedule for most time-based PMs. Use floating only when the next maintenance interval should genuinely depend on when the last job was finished, such as usage-based or condition-driven work. Step 4: Set lead time (optional but recommended) ¤ Lead time tells the system when to create the work order before it's due. Example: Set 7 days lead time. The system creates the work order a week early. This gives you time to get parts and schedule workers. If lead time is too short, parts and labor won't be ready when the work order is generated. If it's left at zero, the work order appears on its due date — leaving no time to prepare. A lead time shorter than your parts procurement time virtually guarantees a delayed job. Step 5: Add the job plan ¤ Link your job plan to the schedule. Each work order will include the same steps and parts list. To change a job plan that is already active, select Revise Job Plan first. For details, see Keep plans current . In practice Organizations often create overly complex schedules at the start, which are hard to maintain Schedules are frequently set up but never activated, so no work orders are generated Lead times are often too short, causing parts shortages and rushed work Teams sometimes create schedules without job plans , leading to inconsistent maintenance What happens next ¤ After you activate the schedule: The system creates work orders automatically Each work order includes your job plan steps Technicians complete the work The system calculates the next due date The system creates the next work order The cycle repeats until you stop it. Common mistakes ¤ Creating too many schedules at once instead of starting with critical equipment Setting unrealistic frequencies (too often or not often enough) Not linking job plans , so technicians don't know what to do Forgetting to activate schedules after creating them Setting lead times that are too short for parts procurement What good looks like ¤ Poor setup Create 50 Preventive Maintenance (PM) schedules for all equipment at once. No job plans . Activate all immediately. Good setup Start with 5-10 critical assets . Create detailed job plans first. Test one schedule. Adjust based on results. Gradually add more equipment. Decision support: Choosing schedule type ¤ Use time-based when: Equipment runs continuously or predictably Manufacturer recommends calendar-based maintenance You need simple, easy-to-manage schedules Use usage-based when: Equipment usage varies significantly Meters are reliable and regularly updated Maintenance depends on actual wear (hours, cycles, miles) Use combined when: You want maintenance to happen even if equipment sits idle Usage is unpredictable You need a safety net for both scenarios Why proper planning matters ¤ If schedules are not set up correctly, equipment fails unexpectedly instead of being maintained proactively If lead times are too short, technicians wait for parts and work gets delayed If job plans are missing, maintenance quality varies and problems are missed Poor scheduling leads to either too much work (overwhelming teams) or too little (equipment failures) If a floating schedule is used and a work order is never closed, no further work orders are generated for that asset — maintenance stops without any alert A schedule left inactive after setup generates no work orders , ever. The first sign is typically an unexpected equipment failure Once your PMs are running, the system takes care of the scheduling — you focus on the work, not the calendar. Continue building your skills ¤ Know what work matters ¤ Create job plans that standardize tasks, parts, and time estimates, then link them to your schedules so technicians always know what to do. How do I decide what work should be done? Schedule your team ¤ Set up calendars and routes so work is assigned when people are available and inspections are grouped efficiently. How do I schedule work? Related topics ¤ How do I decide what work should be done? How do I schedule work? What are the basic concepts? How do I complete a job?

docs.text: How do I schedule work? ¤ Use calendars to set working hours. Use routes to group inspection points. This helps you plan when work happens and organize inspections efficiently. Calendars track when your team works. Routes let you create inspection work orders for multiple items at once. 💡 Tips for success ¤ For calendars: Start simple. Match your standard work week. Add holidays as you go. Update calendars when shifts change. For routes: Group equipment that's close together. Keep routes focused. Don't mix unrelated items . Update routes when equipment changes. Use clear names. Calendars: Set working time ¤ Calendars show when work can happen. They include: Working days and hours Shifts (7 AM - 3 PM, 3 PM - 11 PM) Holidays and shutdowns Days off TODO: Add visual content A diagram showing how calendars connect to labor , locations , and work scheduling would be useful here. When to use calendars ¤ Use calendars to: Set standard work shifts Track holidays and shutdowns Schedule work during available hours Assign work when people are working Calculate realistic finish times How to set up calendars ¤ Step 1: Create shifts Set working days (Monday-Friday) Set start and end times (7:00 AM - 3:00 PM) Enter total work hours per day Step 2: Create the calendar Make a calendar for your organization Add shifts to show the work schedule Mark holidays and days off Step 3: Assign calendars Apply calendars to your team members Apply to locations or equipment if needed System uses calendars to schedule work Assign calendar to Required when Labor records Assigning work to individuals so the system can calculate availability correctly Crews Assigning work to a crew as a group Locations or assets Only when the system needs to calculate scheduled work based on when a location or asset is available, such as for planned shutdowns Routes: Group inspection points ¤ Routes are lists of items that need regular inspection. Create one route. Generate work orders for all items at once. TODO: Add visual content A diagram showing a route with multiple stops and how it generates work orders would be useful here. When to use routes ¤ Use routes for: Regular inspection rounds (daily equipment checks) Safety inspections at multiple locations Maintenance on similar equipment Any work that follows a set path How to set up routes ¤ Step 1: Create the route 1. Open the Routes application 2. Add a clear name (such as "Daily Production Line Inspection") 3. List all items to inspect (called "stops") Step 2: Use the route Add the route to a work order System creates work orders for each stop Add to a maintenance schedule for automatic use Choose: separate work orders or one work order with multiple tasks Option Use when Separate work orders per stop Each stop needs to be tracked, costed, and closed independently — for example, daily checks on Filler FL-02, Spiral Freezer SF-01, and Batch Mixer MX-01 where each job has its own history One work order with multiple tasks All stops are part of a single job and cost tracking at the route level is sufficient Step 3: Complete the work Technicians follow the route They complete inspections at each stop All work tracks under the main work order TODO: Add visual content A video showing how to create a simple inspection route would be useful here. Continue building your skills ¤ Monitor performance ¤ With scheduling in place, track whether work is being completed on time, how much backlog your team carries, and where to intervene. What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ How do I plan recurring maintenance? How do I decide what work should be done? How do I complete a job? How do I assign the correct people?

docs.text: How do I add users? ¤ Before people can work in IBM Maximo Application Suite Select, they need a user account with the correct security group assigned. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Use consistent naming conventions for user IDs Follow principle of least privilege, that is, minimum access needed Keep security group assignments organized What to do ¤ Add a user ¤ Open the Users application. Click Create user . Specify a login email . Specify a user ID . Optionally, add a note in the memo . Example: Temporary access for contractor at ice cream plant A Provide a display name . This is the full name of the user or a recognizable preferred name. Click Select groups and add the user to at least one security group . An email is sent to the login email address. Table 1. Security groups ¤ A security group is a collection of users who share the same access. Security group permissions determine which applications, actions, and data they can access. A role determines what a person can see and do in Maximo Application Suite Select. Assign each user to the security group that matches their role: Security group What they can do System admin Manages system configuration and user access. System administrators can configure domains , communication templates , AI settings, create users, and set up security groups , but typically do not perform day-to-day operational work. Example tasks: Set up notification templates, manage user roles, set up security groups , configure system settings, and maintain data structures. Supervisor Oversees operations and team activities. Supervisors can plan and approve work, review technician work, monitor assets and performance, and access analytics to track progress. Example tasks: Assign and approve work orders , review KPIs, review inspection results, manage job plans , and monitor asset condition and maintenance schedules. Technician Performs maintenance and operational work. Technicians can view and update assigned work, complete inspections, record labor hours, report materials used, and record asset data such as meter readings and condition details. Example tasks: Complete work orders , enter inspection results, update asset condition, record labor hours, report materials used, and report meter readings. Requester Submits and tracks service requests. Requesters have limited access and cannot perform operational or administrative tasks. This role is focused on initiating and monitoring work requests. Example tasks: Create a service request for a broken asset and track its status until it is resolved. Inventory clerk Manages inventory and storeroom operations. Inventory clerks can maintain stock, process item movements, adjust inventory balances, and ensure accurate inventory records. Example tasks: Receive items into inventory , issue materials to work orders , perform inventory counts, adjust inventory balances, and manage storerooms. Note You must assign at least one security group . The user cannot access applications until a security group is assigned. User preferences ¤ Users update their preferences in their profile. They open the profile menu from the top right of the header and can select preferences, such as a default application , storeroom, locale, and language. Continue building your skills ¤ Set up your workforce ¤ After adding users, create the craft and labor records that let you assign work to the correct people. How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? Customize your dropdown values ¤ Add your organization's terminology to status fields and dropdowns so the system speaks your team's language. How do I customize dropdown values? Related topics ¤ How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? How do I assign the correct people? How do I customize dropdown values?

docs.text: How do I automate communication? ¤ Communication templates let you send automatic emails when things happen in the system, such as when a work order changes status or a task is assigned. Push notifications send real-time alerts to mobile devices so field technicians know about new or updated work without having to check the app. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Set the status of a communication template to Active before trying to use it. Inactive templates will not send. Do not edit the built-in system templates. Duplicate an existing template and modify the copy instead. Use roles as recipients rather than hardcoding individual email addresses. Roles resolve dynamically, so notifications reach the correct person even when team membership changes. Test your template by triggering the relevant action on a test record before rolling it out. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Communication terminology ¤ Term What it means Communication template A reusable email template that can be triggered automatically or manually from a record Accessible from Controls where the template can be used: Applications or All Role A dynamic recipient definition that resolves to a person or group at the time the email is sent Substitution variable A placeholder in the template body that pulls live data from the record, such as the work order number Push notification A real-time alert sent to the IBM Maximo Mobile app on a user's mobile device Communication templates ¤ Communication templates automate outbound email for work order assignments, status changes, approvals, and other events. You create a template once, then attach it to an escalation , a workflow, or trigger it manually from a record. How to create a communication template ¤ Go to Administration > Communication Templates . Click New Communication Template . Enter a unique Template ID and a clear description. Set Accessible From to the context where this template will be used (e.g. APPS or ALL ). Enter a Send From email address. This is the address recipients will see as the sender. Enter a Subject line. Use substitution variables to include record data, for example: Work order :wonum has been assigned to you Enter the message body. You can use substitution variables here too, for example :description to include the work order description. Go to the Recipients tab. Add recipients using one or more of the following: Roles : recommended. The role resolves to the correct person at send time. Person groups : sends to group members based on availability. Persons : sends to a specific named person. Email addresses : sends to a fixed address. For each recipient, select To , cc , or bcc . Save the template. Use Change Status to set the template status to Active . Push notifications ¤ Push notifications send real-time alerts to the IBM Maximo Mobile app on iOS and Android devices. Users receive a notification on their device when an event occurs, such as a work order being assigned to them, without needing to have the app open. Setting up push notifications is a two-step process: generate an API key from the IBM push notification portal, then configure it in MAS. Step 1: Generate an API key ¤ Open https://pushnotification.suite.maximo.com in a browser. Sign in with your IBMid. Enter a meaningful name for the API key, for example MAS-PROD-PushNotif . Click Generate API Key . Copy the API key immediately. It will not be shown again once you leave the page. Store it securely. Step 2: Configure push notifications in MAS ¤ In MAS, click the Administration icon and go to Configurations . In the Users and Identity section, click Push Notifications . In the Bundle Identifier field, enter: com.ibm.iot.maximo.mobile In the URL field, enter: https://pushnotification.suite.maximo.com/pushnotification/sendMessage In the API Key field, paste the key you generated in Step 1. Save the configuration. To confirm the setup is working, ask a user to log in via the IBM Maximo Mobile app and trigger a relevant event such as a workflow assignment. The notification should arrive on their device within a few seconds. When users receive push notifications ¤ A user receives push notifications only when all of the following are true: The user has an active session in IBM Maximo Mobile. The user has not signed out of the app. The app has not been reset. If a user's session expires, notifications stop until the user signs in again. The network on the device must also allow connections to the Apple and Google push notification services. [SME confirmation required: Confirm that these conditions apply to MAS Select, including the session length and whether the network must allow connections to the Apple and Google push notification services.] Continue building your skills ¤ Configure Maximo Mobile for field teams ¤ Let technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks use a mobile app to access their work from anywhere. How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? Load your existing data ¤ Now that your configuration is in place, bring in your locations , assets , and inventory from existing records. How do I prepare data for import? Related topics ¤ How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? How do I set up maps? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? Administrator: Add users

docs.text: How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? ¤ IBM Maximo Mobile lets technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks view and complete work, manage inventory , and update records from their mobile device. As an administrator, you configure the defaults that control how mobile devices sync data, which map app your team uses for navigation, and how service requests and work orders behave in the app. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Configure mobile settings before your team downloads and signs in to IBM Maximo Mobile. Changes to defaults apply to all users. Set up Map Manager before configuring mobile map settings. The map app you choose here opens the map that Map Manager provides. Start with the defaults and adjust after your team has used the app in the field. Most settings can be changed at any time. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Data sync options ¤ Each data category offers the same three options. Choose the option that balances data freshness against bandwidth and device storage for your team. Option What it does Reload all data Downloads the full data set each time a sync runs. Use when you need your team to have complete, current data regardless of what changed. Update recent changes Downloads only data that changed since the last sync. Faster and lighter on bandwidth. Suitable for most teams. Do not download data Skips this data category during sync. Use when the data is not needed on the device. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the option labels and where you set them in Select. The Maximo Manage documentation calls the options "Complete", "Only delta", and "Do not download", and lists them under "Worklist data" and "Supporting data" in the Mobile administration app. This page uses "Record data" and "Supporting data".] Before you start ¤ Confirm that your role has permission to update mobile configuration settings in Maximo Application Suite Select. Confirm that Map Manager is configured if you plan to use map navigation. See How do I set up maps? . Confirm that labor records and security groups are set up so technicians can be assigned work. See How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? . [SME confirmation required: Identify which Maximo Application Suite Select roles can update mobile configuration settings.] Open the mobile configuration ¤ [SME confirmation required: Add the confirmed navigation path to mobile configuration in Maximo Application Suite Select. The Maximo Manage path is Administration > Mobile Configuration, but the Maximo Application Suite Select path requires validation.] Choose how mobile data is synchronized ¤ The Default data sync settings section controls what data mobile devices download when a user syncs the app. Configure each category separately. Record data ¤ Record data controls how work orders and service requests are synced to the device. Select one of the three options described in Table 1 . Supporting data ¤ Supporting data controls how lookup data, such as asset records and location lists, is synced to the device. Select one of the three options described in Table 1 . Map data ¤ Map data controls whether map data is downloaded to the device. Select Update recent changes or Reload all data to download map data to devices. Select Do not download data to skip map data during sync. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the exact option labels for map data in the Maximo Application Suite Select design. The Maximo Manage equivalent is a single "Download map data" toggle rather than the three-option model.] Choose the map app ¤ The Map settings section controls which map application IBM Maximo Mobile opens when a user navigates to a location . The available options are: Apple Maps Google Maps Waze Select the map app that your team uses. [SME confirmation required: Confirm whether map app options are platform-specific (for example, Apple Maps on iOS only) or available on all supported platforms. Confirm whether a browser fallback option appears in the final Maximo Application Suite Select design.] Configure service request behavior ¤ The SR mobile settings section controls how the service request experience works in IBM Maximo Mobile. Enable follow similar requests ¤ Enable follow similar requests allows technicians to see service requests that are similar to the one they are creating or viewing. Turn this setting on or off depending on whether your team uses this feature. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the exact effect of enabling or disabling this setting, and whether "similar requests" is defined by a matching location, asset, description, or another criterion.] Service address priority ¤ Service address priority determines which address IBM Maximo Mobile uses when a service request has more than one address associated with it. Select the priority value that reflects how your organization resolves address conflicts. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the available priority values and their order of precedence in the final Maximo Application Suite Select design.] Enable show all systems ¤ Enable show all systems controls whether technicians can see all systems when creating or viewing a service request. Turn this setting on or off depending on whether your team needs access to all systems. [SME confirmation required: Confirm what "systems" refers to in the Maximo Application Suite Select context and the effect of enabling or disabling this setting.] Configure work order behavior ¤ Two sections control how work orders behave in IBM Maximo Mobile: Work order status and Miscellaneous settings . Work order status ¤ Work order status controls which status values are available to technicians when they update a work order in the app. Complete status sets the status value that IBM Maximo Mobile applies when a technician marks a work order as complete. [SME confirmation required: Confirm whether COMP is the default complete status value in the Maximo Application Suite Select design, and whether technicians see the status code or a plain-language label.] Allow go to report work ¤ Allow go to report work controls whether technicians see an option to navigate to the report work view from the work order . Turn this on if your team records labor , materials, or other actuals directly against work orders in the mobile app. [SME confirmation required: Confirm the exact label used in the Maximo Application Suite Select interface for the report work view. Do not use "Report Works" or "Actuals" unless those terms appear in the final product interface.] Date attributes ¤ The Miscellaneous settings section includes settings that control which date attributes are visible in the app. [SME confirmation required: Confirm which date attributes are exposed in the Maximo Application Suite Select design (for example, scheduled start, scheduled finish, target start) and whether the SCHEDULE default selection is confirmed in the final design.] Configure travel guidance ¤ [SME confirmation required: Confirm whether travel settings are exposed and supported in Maximo Application Suite Select. If confirmed, document Enable travel prompt and Travel radius. Do not describe triggers, measurement units, or geographic data requirements unless they are confirmed in the final design.] What to do next ¤ After you configure IBM Maximo Mobile, prepare your team to use it: How do I automate communication? : Set up real-time push notifications so field technicians receive alerts on their mobile devices when work is assigned. How do I complete a work order ? : Understand what technicians experience when completing work in the app. How do I find my work? : See how technicians and supervisors access their work queue in IBM Maximo Mobile. Share with your team ¤ Send technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks to How do I get IBM Maximo Mobile? for download and sign-in instructions. Continue building your skills ¤ Load your existing data ¤ With your system configured, bring in your locations , assets , and inventory records. How do I prepare data for import? Related topics ¤ How do I set up maps? How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? How do I automate communication? Administrator: Add users

docs.text: What is the correct load order? ¤ Import order matters. Referenced records must exist before records that use them, and parent records must exist before child records. TODO: Add visual content A diagram showing the dependency chain (reference data → locations → assets → work orders ) would be useful here. Why does load order matter? ¤ Child records reference parent records. If the parent doesn't exist yet, the child import will fail. Similarly, if a record references supporting data that doesn't exist, the import will fail. Example : You can't create "Ice Cream Plant A > Production Building > Filling Line 2" if "Ice Cream Plant A" and "Production Building" don't exist. Recommended import order ¤ 1. Reference data used by locations and assets ¤ Import supporting records before importing locations or assets that reference them. What to import first : GL accounts Service addresses Calendars and shifts Failure classes Vendors and manufacturers Asset type values Classifications and specifications Site addresses (bill-to and ship-to) Why this matters : Locations and assets reference these records. If the referenced data doesn't exist, the import will fail. 2. Locations (in hierarchy order) ¤ Import locations from top to bottom of the hierarchy: Top-level locations first (Ice Cream Plant A) Second-level locations next (Production Building) Lowest-level locations last (Filling Line 2) What to check : Verify the location hierarchy before importing Import parent locations before child locations Confirm that system location references use valid values Confirm that each child location references the correct parent Import hierarchies sequentially Hierarchies require sequential loading (top → down). Import parent locations first, then their children. 3. Assets (including parent-child relationships) ¤ Import assets after their locations exist. What to check : Location references are valid Parent assets exist (if using asset hierarchies) For asset hierarchies : Import parent assets before child assets or subassemblies Verify that each child asset references the correct parent asset Verify that the parent asset exists at the expected site and, if applicable, location 4. Other records that reference locations or assets ¤ Import other records that depend on locations and assets : Work orders (reference assets and locations ) Inventory (reference locations ) Common hierarchy patterns ¤ Location hierarchies ¤ Correct order : 1. Site (Ice Cream Plant A) 2. Building (Production Building) 3. Area (Filling Line 2) 4. Sub-area (if applicable) What happens if you import in wrong order : Child locations fail because their parent doesn't exist. What to do : Sort your import file so parent records come before child records. Asset hierarchies ¤ If using parent-child asset relationships: Correct order : 1. Parent assets 2. Child assets or subassemblies What to check : Parent asset IDs are correct Each child asset references the correct parent Parent assets exist at the expected site and location Parent-child relationships ¤ General rule : Always import parents before children. What to check : Parent location IDs are correct Hierarchy levels are properly defined System location references are valid What to do : Verify all parent records exist before importing child records. What happens next? ¤ After understanding load order: Plan your import sequence Import reference data first Prepare data files in the correct order Import parent records before children Verify parents were created successfully Import child records Continue building your skills ¤ Run the import ¤ With your data in the correct order, you're ready to import it into the system. How do I get data into the system? Fix errors when an import fails ¤ Some failures are about order and dependency. Learn how to read the error report and resolve problems. How do I fix import errors? docs.text: How do I get data into the system? ¤ Use Data Management to import your existing records into IBM Maximo Application Suite Select from a CSV file. This is how you bring in locations , assets , items , and other data in bulk during setup, or any time you need to add or update a large number of records. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Always download the export template first. The template shows you the exact column names and format the system expects. Keep your CSV file under 500 KB. Larger files need to be split into smaller batches. Import one data type at a time, in the correct sequence. See What is the correct load order? for the import sequence. Format ID columns as text in your spreadsheet application before entering data. Spreadsheet applications such as Microsoft Excel can silently reformat IDs as numbers, which breaks the import. Run a small test batch of 5–10 records before importing hundreds. This lets you catch format problems quickly. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. What you can import ¤ Data type When to import Locations Sites , buildings, areas, and functional locations where assets are installed Assets Equipment and infrastructure your organization maintains Items Inventory parts and materials stocked in your storeroom GL accounts Cost codes and account structures How to get the correct template ¤ Before filling in your data, export an existing record to get a template with the correct column names and format. What to do: Open the application that matches the data you want to import. For example, open the Assets application to get an assets template. Search for and open any existing record. Click the download icon or Export data . In the Export data window, select Export custom columns . In the Template name field, select the object structure that matches your data type. Click Export . The file downloads as a CSV. Open the file in a spreadsheet application to see the required columns and their format. Do not enter a value in the Template name field when exporting. Leave it blank to get the default structure. Note If no records exist yet, your system administrator can provide a template directly, or you can find the required fields in How do I prepare data for import? . How to import your data ¤ Once your CSV file is prepared and validated: What to do: Open the application where you want to import data. For example, open the Assets application to import assets . Click the upload icon or Import data . In the Import data window, select the object structure that matches your file. Click Browse and select your prepared CSV file. Select Import preview to check for errors before committing the import. Review any errors flagged in the preview. Fix the issues in your CSV file and upload again if needed. Once the preview is clean, clear Import preview and click Import to run the full import. Click the number in Total rows to go to the application and review your imported records. [SME confirmation required: confirm exact UI labels for Import data button and Import preview checkbox in MAS Select — these may differ from Maximo Manage] What happens during import ¤ When you import a file, the system: Reads each row in your CSV Validates each field against system rules Creates or updates the records Reports any rows that failed, with the reason Failed rows do not stop the rest of the import. The system processes every row and reports failures at the end. How to fix import errors ¤ After importing, review the error report: Missing required field : A column that the system requires was blank. Fill in the value and re-import that row. Invalid value : A field contained a value that doesn't match the system's valid values. For example, a status code that doesn't exist, or a site ID that isn't set up yet. Record already exists : You are trying to create a record with an ID that already exists. Either update the existing record instead, or use a different ID. Parent record not found : A referenced record doesn't exist yet. Import the parent record first. See What is the correct load order? . For a full list of import error causes and fixes, see How do I fix import errors? . File size limits ¤ The maximum file size for a single import is 500 KB. If your data exceeds 500 KB: Split the file into smaller batches. Import each batch separately, in the same order. Wait for each batch to complete before importing the next. [SME confirmation required: confirm the 500 KB limit applies in MAS Select — sourced from IBM Docs for MAS 9.1 but may differ in MAS Select SaaS context] Continue building your skills ¤ Fix errors when an import fails ¤ Not every import goes smoothly. Learn how to read the error report and correct common problems. How do I fix import errors? Verify the system is working ¤ Once your data is in, check whether the system is performing as expected. What metrics matter? Related topics ¤ How do I prepare data for import? What is the correct load order? How do I fix import errors? Administrator: Add users

docs.text: Which object structure do I use for each data type? ¤ When you import data into Maximo Application Suite Select, you use an object structure to define what you're loading. Think of an object structure as a spreadsheet template that defines the columns available for a particular type of data, such as assets or locations . You pick the template that matches what you're loading, then fill it with your data. Use this reference to find the correct object structure for each data type. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Object structure by data type ¤ [SME confirmation required: Verify all object structure names against the Maximo Application Suite Select Data Management application before publishing. Names noted with * are unconfirmed and may differ from standard Maximo Manage names.] Data type Object structure Notes Asset MXAPIASSET Use for importing asset records, including asset numbers, descriptions, locations , and classifications. [SME confirmation required: Confirm whether MXAPIASSET or MXAPIASSETS is the correct name in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Inventory MXAPIINVENTORY [SME confirmation required: Confirm the correct object structure name and usage for inventory imports in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Item MXAPIITEM [SME confirmation required: Confirm the correct object structure name and usage for item imports in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Job plan MXAPIJOBPLAN [SME confirmation required: Confirm the correct object structure name and usage for job plan imports in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Labor MXAPILABOR [SME confirmation required: Confirm the correct object structure name and usage for labor imports in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Location MXAPIOPERLOC Use for importing operating locations and location hierarchies. [SME confirmation required: Confirm whether MXAPIOPERLOC or MXOPERLOC is the correct name in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Meter MXAPIMETER [SME confirmation required: Confirm the correct object structure name and usage for meter imports in Maximo Application Suite Select.] PM/Master PM MXAPIPM [SME confirmation required: Confirm the correct object structure name and usage for PM and Master PM imports in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Service Item MXAPISERVITEM [SME confirmation required: Confirm the correct object structure name and usage for service item imports in Maximo Application Suite Select.] Common fields by data type ¤ Assets ( MXAPIASSET ) ¤ [SME confirmation required: Confirm the required and commonly used fields for asset imports in Maximo Application Suite Select. The following are common fields in standard Maximo Manage and require validation.] Field Description Required ASSETNUM Unique identifier for the asset Yes SITEID The site the asset belongs to Yes DESCRIPTION Short description of the asset Recommended LOCATION The operating location of the asset No ASSETTYPE The asset type classification No STATUS Asset status , such as OPERATING or DECOMMISSIONED No SERIALNUM Serial number of the asset No VENDOR Vendor or manufacturer name No Locations ( MXAPIOPERLOC ) ¤ [SME confirmation required: Confirm the required and commonly used fields for location imports in Maximo Application Suite Select. The following are common fields in standard Maximo Manage and require validation.] Field Description Required LOCATION Unique identifier for the location Yes SITEID The site the location belongs to Yes DESCRIPTION Short description of the location Recommended TYPE Location type, such as OPERATING Yes PARENT Parent location identifier for hierarchy No STATUS Location status , such as OPERATING No What to do next ¤ How do I prepare data for import? : Format your import file correctly before loading data. What is the correct load order? : Import data in the correct sequence to avoid reference errors. How do I fix import errors? : Troubleshoot common import failures. docs.text: How do I prepare data for import? ¤ Proper data preparation prevents import failures and ensures data quality. TODO: Add visual content A screenshot showing a well-formatted import file would be useful here. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Start with a template : Export existing records to see correct format Validate data first : Check all values against system data Use text format : Prevent Excel from corrupting data Test with small batches : Verify format before importing thousands of records Keep error logs : Document what went wrong for future imports Common preparation steps ¤ Use the correct file format ¤ What to do : Save files as CSV (Comma delimited) format Use UTF-8 encoding for special characters Format ID columns as text in Excel before entering data Validate field names and structure ¤ What to check : Column names match system field names exactly All required fields are included Field names are correct (case-sensitive) What to do : Use a template or export an existing record to see the correct structure. Prevent Excel from corrupting data ¤ Excel can corrupt data in several ways: Dates : Converts text to dates (01-02 becomes Jan 2) IDs : Removes leading zeros (001 becomes 1) Long numbers : Converts to scientific notation What to do : Format all columns as text in Excel before entering data, or use a plain text editor to create the CSV. TODO: Add visual content A screenshot showing Excel formatting options (Format Cells → Text) would be helpful. Clean your data ¤ What to check : Remove extra spaces from all fields Ensure consistent formatting Validate data against system values ( status codes, site IDs, etc.) Check for duplicate IDs Check referenced data before importing ¤ Verify that supporting records exist before importing locations or assets . Missing referenced data is a common cause of import failures. For location imports ¤ What to check : Field Required when GL accounts Your organization tracks maintenance costs by cost centre Service addresses Locations need to appear on maps or work order dispatch Calendars and shifts Scheduling work or calculating availability at this location Failure classes You want structured failure reporting on work orders for this location Classifications and specifications You want to search or report on locations by equipment type What to do : Create missing referenced records before importing locations , or update the import file to use existing values. For asset imports ¤ What to check : Field Required when GL accounts Tracking maintenance costs by cost centre Service addresses Assets need to appear on maps or work order dispatch Failure classes Technicians need to select failure codes on work orders for this asset — without this, the Failure Reporting tab is empty Rotating items Only when the asset is a rotating, serialised item tracked by individual asset record Vendors and manufacturers Tracking warranty, procurement, or service history by supplier Classifications and specifications You want to search, filter, or report on assets by type or specification What to do : Verify all referenced records exist before importing assets . Create missing records or correct values in the import file. Use consistent date formats ¤ Date formats are a common source of import errors. Follow these guidelines to prevent date-related failures. What to do : Use one accepted date format consistently throughout the file Do not mix regional date formats (for example, MM/DD/YYYY and DD/MM/YYYY) Avoid ambiguous dates such as 01/02/2026 unless the accepted format is clear Format date columns as text in Excel before entering values Test a small batch that includes date values before importing the full file Common date format issues : Excel automatically converts dates to its default format Mixed formats cause some records to fail while others succeed Ambiguous dates are interpreted incorrectly What to do : Verify the expected date format for your system and apply it consistently to all date fields. Import hierarchies in the correct order ¤ For locations and parent-child relationships: What to do : Import in order: Top-level records first (parents) Second-level records next Lowest-level records last (children) Break large imports into batches ¤ What to do : Break files into smaller batches (1,000-5,000 records at a time) This prevents timeouts and makes troubleshooting easier Preview before importing ¤ Use preview/import validation : Always preview your import before committing it. This shows: Which records will succeed Which records will fail What errors need to be fixed TODO: Add visual content A screenshot of the import preview screen showing validation results would be useful here. Without validation If you skip validation, errors are only discovered after processing. This can result in: Partial imports with missing records Incorrect data in the system Time wasted troubleshooting after the fact What happens next? ¤ After preparing your data: Preview the import to validate Fix any errors identified Process the import Verify records were created successfully Continue building your skills ¤ Get the sequence right before you import ¤ Import order matters. Learn which data types need to be loaded before others. What is the correct load order? Run the import ¤ With your data prepared, run the import. How do I get data into the system? docs.text: How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? ¤ Set up your workforce resources before you start assigning work. Crafts define the skills in your organization. Labor records represent the people. Crews group people together so you can assign a whole team to a job in one step. These records work together. You need to set them up in the correct order. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Set up crafts before labor . A labor record must reference a valid craft . Set up a calendar before creating a crew . The crew 's calendar controls when its members show as available. Match the calendar and shift on each labor record to the crew they belong to. A mismatch is the most common reason crew members show as unavailable when you try to assign work. Leave the End Date blank on labor assignments to a crew unless the assignment has a fixed end. This keeps the member permanently assigned until you need to change it. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Labor and crew terminology ¤ Term What it means Craft A skill or trade, such as Electrician or Mechanic, used to match the correct person to the correct job Calendar Defines working days and shifts. Must be assigned to both the crew and each member. Labor A person who performs work or records time, linked to a person record in the system Crew type A template that defines the positions and crafts a crew requires, such as Leader and Helper Crew A named group of people assembled to work together, built from a crew type Setup order ¤ Set these up in sequence. Each step depends on the one before it. Crafts → Calendar → Labor → Crew type → Crew Step 1: Create crafts ¤ Crafts represent the skills in your workforce. Go to Resources > Crafts . Create a new craft record. Enter a craft ID and description, for example, MECH, Mechanic or REFRIG, Refrigeration technician . Set the default rate if applicable. Save. Repeat for each skill type in your organization. Step 2: Set up a calendar ¤ Crews need a calendar to define when their members are available. If you have not already created a calendar for your workforce, do this before creating crew types. See How do I schedule work? for steps to create shifts and calendars. Step 3: Create labor records ¤ Labor records represent the individuals who perform work. Go to Resources > Labor . Create a new labor record. Link it to the person's existing person record. In the Crafts section, add the person's craft and set it as their default craft . The Available Labor dialog filters by default craft only — a person with the correct skill listed as a secondary craft will not appear when supervisors search for available people. Set the same calendar and shift you plan to use for the crew they will join. If these differ from the crew 's calendar, the person will show as unavailable every time a supervisor or scheduler tries to assign them — even when they are physically at work. Save. Repeat for each person in your workforce. Step 4: Create a crew type ¤ A crew type is the template for a crew . It defines the positions and crafts required. Go to Resources > Crews . From the Crew Types tab, create a new crew type. In the Required Crafts section, add each position with its craft : Add a Leader position and assign the relevant craft Add any Helper or other positions required Save. Step 5: Create a crew ¤ With the crew type, crafts , calendar, and labor records in place, you can now create a crew . Go to Resources > Crews . Create a new crew . Select the crew type you created. Assign the calendar the crew will work to. Go to the Labor Assignments tab. Add each team member: Select the position (for example, Leader) Select the labor record The Effective Date defaults to the start of today's shift. Adjust if needed. Leave End Date blank for a permanent assignment. If an End Date lapses, the crew member is silently dropped from availability — work can no longer be assigned to that crew , with no system warning. Save. Common issues ¤ Crew members showing as "Not available" ¤ The most common cause is a mismatch between the crew 's calendar and the calendar assigned to the individual labor records. The system calculates availability from the labor record's calendar and shift — not the crew 's. Even if the crew calendar is correct, a technician will appear unavailable if their personal labor record uses a different calendar. Check that both use the same calendar and shift. " Craft mismatch" warning when adding labor to a crew ¤ The labor record does not have the craft required for that crew position. Go to the labor record, add the correct craft in the Crafts section, then return to the crew assignment. Work can't be assigned to a crew ¤ The crew must have at least one labor member assigned with a valid Effective Date and no expired End Date. Check the Labor Assignments tab for any assignments where the End Date has passed. What to do next ¤ Once labor , crafts , and crews are set up: How do I assign the correct people? : Assign labor or crews to work orders . How do I plan recurring maintenance? : Add labor requirements to job plans . How do I schedule work? : Use calendars and routes to organize your team's work. Continue building your skills ¤ Customize your dropdown values ¤ Add your organization's terminology to status fields and dropdowns so the system uses your team's language. How do I customize dropdown values? Set up maps ¤ Once your workforce is configured, set up a map so field teams can see asset and work order locations visually. How do I set up maps? Related topics ¤ How do I schedule work? How do I assign the correct people? How do I standardize data?

docs.text: How do I set up maps? ¤ Map Manager lets you configure a map so that users can see the location of assets , work orders , and service addresses on a visual map inside the application. Once a map is configured and enabled, it appears in spatially enabled applications for all users. 💡 Tips for success ¤ Keep your first map simple. One basemap service is enough to get started. You can add more map services later. Use a descriptive name for each map service so it is easy to identify if you add more later. If users will be viewing maps on mobile devices, use the same map configuration. Mobile users see the same map as desktop users. Quick reference ¤ Table 1. Map terminology ¤ Term What it means Map Manager The application where you create and configure maps Map provider The mapping service that supplies the background map, such as OpenMap Basemap The background map layer that shows geography, streets, or satellite imagery Map service A URL that points to a map tile or layer from your map provider Initial extent The default view that opens when a user first opens the map What you need before you start ¤ A basemap URL from your map provider. OpenMap supports public ArcGIS basemap URLs, which do not require an account or license to use. The name of the applications you want maps to appear in. How to set up a map ¤ Go to Administration > Map Manager . Click New Map . Enter a unique name and a short description for the map. Select Enable Map to activate this configuration. Set the Map Provider to OpenMap . In the Map Services table, click Add Row . Enter a name for the map service, for example, Basemap . Enter the basemap URL. For example, to use a public ArcGIS basemap : https://services.arcgisonline.com/ArcGIS/rest/services/World_Street_Map/MapServer Set the Order value. The basemap should have the highest order value in the list. Set the Initial Extent for the map. Pan and zoom to the geographic area your organization works in, then save the extent. Save the map record. Confirm the map is working ¤ After saving, open the Locations or Assets application and open a record that has a location or address. A map panel should appear on the record showing your configured basemap . If the map does not appear, check that: The map record has Enable Map selected. The basemap URL is accessible from the application. If your map does not load In some environments, the application's security policy may block external map tile servers. If the map panel appears but the map does not load, contact IBM support. In Maximo Application Suite Select, system-level security settings are managed by IBM. Continue building your skills ¤ Automate your notifications ¤ With your map in place, keep your team informed. Set up email and push notifications so people know when work is assigned or updated. How do I automate communication? Configure Maximo Mobile for field teams ¤ Let technicians, supervisors, and inventory clerks use a mobile app to access their work from anywhere. How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team? Related topics ¤ How do I set up labor , crafts , and crews ? How do I automate communication? How do I configure IBM Maximo Mobile for my team?
